components.name: TAFC
components.description: TAFC (Temenos Application Framework C) was the C-based runtime environment for T24 and Globus from 2000 to 2020. It executed compiled InfoBasic code and provided database abstraction, enabling platform independence across Windows, Unix, and Linux systems. TAFC interfaced with JBase and other MultiValue databases using the DC Driver for data access. The runtime managed session handling, transaction processing, and resource management for banking operations. TAFC supported deployment on multiple operating systems including Windows, AIX, z Series (OS/390), i Series, and various Unix flavors. It was gradually superseded by TAFJ (Java-based runtime) starting in 2011, with TAFC support ending in 2020.

components.name: TC Server
components.description: TC Server (Temenos Connect Server) was the JEE application server component used from 2004 to 2011 during the early T24 era. It provided the connectivity layer between web interfaces and the T24 core banking system, handling HTTP requests and session management. TC Server enabled browser-based access to T24 functionality, supporting the transition from desktop clients to web applications. The server managed connection pooling, security authentication, and request routing to the TAFC runtime. TC Server was replaced by TOCF (Temenos Open Connectivity Framework) in 2009, which provided enhanced JEE application server integration with WebSphere, WebLogic, and JBoss platforms.

components.name: TOCF (JEE)
components.description: TOCF (Temenos Open Connectivity Framework) is the JEE connectivity layer introduced in 2009 and still active today. It provides integration between JEE application servers and the Transact/T24 core banking engine through EJB (Enterprise JavaBeans) interfaces. TOCF manages connection pooling, transaction coordination, and security integration across WebSphere, WebLogic, and JBoss application servers. The framework handles OFS message processing, session management, and resource allocation for concurrent banking operations. TOCF enables enterprise deployment patterns with load balancing, failover, and clustering capabilities. It works with both TAFC (historical) and TAFJ runtimes, serving as the standard application server integration layer for Temenos deployments.

components.name: TAFJ
components.description: TAFJ (Temenos Application Framework for Java) is the Java-based runtime environment introduced in 2011, serving as the current standard platform for Transact execution. It compiles InfoBasic code to Java bytecode, enabling platform independence across any JVM-compatible system. TAFJ provides multi-threading support, JDBC database connectivity, and integration with JEE application servers. The runtime includes thread management, memory management, caching services, and session handling for high-performance banking operations. TAFJ supports all major databases through JDBC including Oracle, DB2, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and cloud databases. Container deployment on Kubernetes became possible with TAFJ, enabling modern cloud-native architectures for Transact deployments.

components.name: TAF.NET
components.description: TAF.NET (Temenos Application Framework for .NET) was a short-lived runtime environment introduced in 2013 that enabled T24 execution on Microsoft .NET infrastructure. It aimed to provide an alternative to the Java-based TAFJ for organizations heavily invested in Microsoft technology stacks. TAF.NET compiled InfoBasic code into .NET assemblies running on the CLR (Common Language Runtime), integrating with SQL Server and Windows Server deployments. However, the framework was discontinued in 2014 due to limited adoption and the strategic focus on TAFJ as the primary runtime. The brief TAF.NET experiment demonstrated the complexity of maintaining multiple runtime environments while TAFJ consolidated as the standard platform.

components.name: COB 24x7
components.description: COB 24x7 (Close of Business 24x7) is a continuous operations capability introduced in 2003 that enables banks to maintain online services during end-of-day batch processing. Traditional batch processing required system downtime, but COB 24x7 allows parallel execution of batch jobs while online transactions continue. It uses transaction queuing, parallel processing, and state management to minimize disruption. This capability is essential for global banks operating across time zones and for digital banking channels requiring round-the-clock availability.

components.name: TSA
components.description: TSA (Temenos Service Agent) was introduced in 2002 as a component within Temenos to enable background services to run concurrently with online processing. It leveraged multithreading capabilities to facilitate parallel processing of tasks, enhancing system efficiency and responsiveness. TSA processes could be initiated through the user interface or programmatically via an API. As a standard feature, TSA included out-of-the-box processes supporting various banking operations, and developers could create new TSA processes using the Java programmatic API. TSA was replaced by TSA 2.0 in 2020.

components.name: TSA 2.0
components.description: TSA 2.0 (Temenos Service Agent 2.0) is the modernized service agent component introduced in 2020, replacing the original TSA. It enables background services to run concurrently with online processing within Temenos Transact, leveraging enhanced multithreading for parallel task execution. TSA 2.0 maintains high system performance and availability, ensuring batch and maintenance operations do not interfere with customer-facing activities. It supports cloud-native deployment patterns including Kubernetes orchestration, while providing backward compatibility for existing TSA processes migrating from the original implementation.

components.name: Process Workflow
components.description: Process Workflow is Temenos's business process automation component introduced in 2005. It enables banks to define, execute, and monitor complex business workflows across the banking platform. The module supports workflow definition with configurable task routing, approval chains, and SLA monitoring. It integrates tightly with T24/Transact transactions, allowing multi-step approval processes, exception handling, and workload distribution. Process Workflow includes PW Designer for visual workflow creation and supports both automated and manual task assignments for compliance and operational processes.

components.name: Multi-Company
components.description: Multi-Company is a core T24/Transact capability introduced in 2005 that enables a single installation to support multiple legal entities or subsidiaries within one banking group. Each company maintains separate books, accounting records, customer data, and configuration parameters while sharing the same application codebase. The Security Management System controls access based on company assignment, ensuring users only see data for authorized entities. Headquarters can access all company books while subsidiaries see only their own data. Multi-Company supports synchronized Close of Business across entities, inter-company transactions, and consolidated reporting. This capability differs from Multi-Tenant in that it serves multiple entities within ONE bank, rather than multiple separate banks.

components.name: Global Processing
components.description: Global Processing (GP) is a T24/Transact capability introduced in 2006 that enables independent operation of companies within a single Temenos Transact environment. Building on the Multi-Company feature, GP allows Close of Business (COB) processing for specific companies while other companies continue online transaction processing. This capability is essential for implementations spanning multiple geographical locations with different time zones, where each region needs to complete its end-of-day batch processing independently. GP enables a subsidiary in Asia to run COB while European operations remain online, ensuring continuous global operations without forcing system-wide batch windows.

components.name: Multi-Tenant
components.description: Multi-Tenant was a deployment architecture introduced in 2015 (v1) enabling multiple separate financial institutions to share a single T24/Transact installation while maintaining complete data isolation. Unlike Multi-Company (multiple entities within one bank), Multi-Tenant served multiple separate banks on shared infrastructure. Each tenant had their own database with individual backup/restore, while sharing application servers and codebase. Multi-Tenant v1 (2015) provided central administration, tenant grouping, and master data management. Multi-Tenant v2 (2019) added cloud-native capabilities with tenant identification at entry point. The capability was abandoned in 2021 due to limited market adoption, as most banks preferred dedicated deployments or moved directly to SaaS offerings rather than shared multi-tenant infrastructure.

components.name: Online Upgrades
components.description: Online Upgrades capability was introduced in 2018 to enable zero-downtime system updates for T24/Transact deployments. This feature allows application updates, patches, and configuration changes while the banking system remains operational, eliminating maintenance windows that disrupt customer services. Online Upgrades utilizes rolling deployment strategies with transaction queuing to ensure no in-flight transactions are lost during updates. The capability became essential for SaaS deployments where maintenance windows are unacceptable and for banks operating globally across time zones. This evolved into the Continuous Updates framework in 2024 with automated testing and rollback capabilities.

components.name: Arrangement Architecture
components.description: Arrangement Architecture is Temenos's revolutionary product configuration framework introduced in 2009. It transforms banking product management from code-based to configuration-based, enabling banks to create and modify products without development effort. AA uses component-based design with property inheritance, event-driven processing, and lifecycle management. Products are defined as templates with mandatory and optional components, while arrangements represent specific product instances held by customers. The framework supports backward and forward-dated events, reversal and replay processing, and provides comprehensive audit trails. AA Designer provides visual tools for product configuration and simulation.

components.name: Alerts
components.description: Alerts is an event-based notification system introduced in 2010 for T24/Transact. It enables banks to configure and deliver customer and operational alerts based on predefined trigger conditions. The module supports multiple delivery channels including SMS, email, push notifications, and in-app messages. Alerts can be triggered by balance thresholds, transaction patterns, account status changes, payment deadlines, and custom business rules. Banks can define alert templates, personalization rules, and customer preferences for notification frequency and delivery methods.

components.name: ProDB
components.description: ProDB was an enterprise data management solution introduced in 2007 for centralized management of reference and market data related to financial instruments. It managed static data, corporate actions, and pricing information critical for financial institutions, especially in private banking. ProDB operated on a meta-model architecture where all entities and attributes were defined, enabling extensive customization. It included a rules engine that validated and consolidated data from various providers, producing a consistent 'golden copy' of data. ProDB was rebranded and enhanced as Temenos DataSource in 2012.

components.name: Data Source
components.description: Temenos DataSource (formerly ProDB) is an enterprise data management solution for centralized management of reference and market data related to financial instruments. It manages static data, corporate actions, and pricing information critical for financial institutions. DataSource operates on a meta-model architecture enabling extensive customization without impacting upgrades. Its rules engine validates and consolidates data from international and local providers, producing a consistent 'golden copy' for distribution across the organization. DataSource integrates with Temenos Transact, Triple A (TAP), and Multifonds, supporting SaaS, on-premises, and cloud deployments. It provides APIs via the TDS Packager API for configuration and customization.

components.name: FCM
components.description: FCM (Financial Crime Mitigation) is Temenos's compliance and risk management module introduced in 2010. It provides comprehensive capabilities for detecting and preventing financial crimes including money laundering, fraud, and sanctions violations. FCM integrates with core banking transactions to perform real-time screening, suspicious activity monitoring, and case management. The module supports configurable risk scoring, watchlist screening, transaction monitoring rules, and regulatory reporting. It helps banks meet AML/KYC compliance requirements across multiple jurisdictions.

components.name: Insight and Analytics
components.description: Insight and Analytics is Temenos' business intelligence and analytics platform providing comprehensive reporting, dashboards, and analytical capabilities for banking operations. Originally introduced as Insight (2009), it evolved through Embedded Analytics (2016) to the current Analytics platform (2017). The solution provides pre-built dashboards, custom report builders, predictive analytics, and in-application visualizations. It integrates with DES and Data Hub for real-time and historical data analysis, supporting regulatory reporting, customer insights, risk monitoring, and operational metrics. The platform enables drill-down capabilities for operational and strategic decision-making across Transact and Infinity.

components.name: TAP
components.description: TAP (Triple A Plus) is a wealth management and private banking platform that came to Temenos through the Odyssey acquisition in 2008. It provides comprehensive wealth management capabilities including portfolio management, investment advisory, client relationship management, and private banking services. TAP integrates with T24/Transact core banking through the TTI (TAP T24 Interface) to access account information, execute transactions, and synchronize client data. The platform supports high-net-worth individual servicing, discretionary and advisory portfolio management, and regulatory compliance for wealth management operations.

components.name: TTI
components.description: TTI (TAP T24 Interface) is an interface component introduced in 2014 that provides connectivity between TAP (Triple A Plus wealth management platform) and T24/Transact core banking. It serves as the integration bridge enabling the TAP wealth platform to communicate with the core banking system for transaction processing, account access, and data synchronization. TTI handles message translation, transaction routing, and response handling between the wealth management layer and core banking. The interface ensures consistent data exchange and transaction integrity, supporting the channel architecture where TAP manages wealth and private banking interactions while T24/Transact processes the underlying banking transactions.

components.name: Wealth Manager
components.description: Wealth Manager was a specialized module introduced in 2010 for wealth management and private banking operations within T24. It provided portfolio management, investment tracking, client reporting, and relationship manager tools. The module supported discretionary and advisory portfolio services, performance measurement, and regulatory reporting for wealth clients. Wealth Manager was deprecated in 2017 as Temenos evolved its wealth management offerings toward more specialized solutions.

components.name: DLM
components.description: DLM (Data Lifecycle Management) is a data governance component introduced in 2015 for managing the complete lifecycle of data within T24/Transact systems. It handles data archival, retention policies, purging, and compliance with regulatory requirements for data storage periods. DLM supports configurable retention rules based on data type, regulatory jurisdiction, and business needs. The module enables banks to optimize storage costs while maintaining audit trails and meeting legal requirements for data preservation and deletion.

components.name: TPS
components.description: TPS (Temenos Payment Services) was a dedicated payments processing system introduced in 2014 for managing payment transactions within T24. It provided centralized payment processing, routing, and clearing integration for domestic and international transfers. TPS supported multiple payment types, message formats, and regulatory requirements. The component was replaced by TPH (Temenos Payments Hub) in 2018, which offered more comprehensive payment orchestration and modern integration capabilities.

components.name: TPH
components.description: TPH (Temenos Payments Hub) is the modern payments processing platform introduced in 2018, replacing TPS (Temenos Payment Services). It provides centralized payment processing across multiple payment types, channels, and clearing networks. TPH supports domestic and international transfers, instant payments, batch processing, and regulatory compliance including PSD2 and ISO 20022. The hub offers payment orchestration, routing optimization, exception handling, and comprehensive reporting. It integrates with SWIFT, local clearing systems, and real-time payment networks.

components.name: PEMINT
components.description: PEMINT (Payment Engine Integration) is a payment integration component introduced in 2020 that facilitates connectivity between Transact and external payment systems. It provides standardized interfaces for integrating with various payment networks, clearing houses, and third-party payment processors. PEMINT supports message transformation, protocol translation, and routing logic for different payment types. The component enables banks to connect to multiple payment infrastructures while maintaining consistent internal processing and reconciliation.

components.name: TAC
components.description: TAC (Temenos Advanced Collections) is a collections management solution acquired by Temenos in 2017. It automates and streamlines the entire collections and arrears process for loans and overdue payments. TAC provides a highly configurable dunning process with automatic creation of collection items for overdue loans, ensuring collection agents receive timely alerts. Banks can define multiple aging stages (arrears at 15, 30, 60 days, grace periods, delinquency, non-accrual status) with distinct actions for each step including automatic penalty interest calculation, customer reminders, and automatic transition to non-accrual status. The solution supports detailed tracking of collection activities with comprehensive audit trails and case management, integrating with core banking for real-time visibility and control over recovery efforts.

components.name: Data Lake & Data Hub
components.description: Data Lake & Data Hub is Temenos' enterprise data platform for centralized banking data management. Introduced as Data Lake in 2019 and evolved into the unified Data Hub in 2023, it provides a comprehensive data repository supporting raw, processed, and curated banking data at scale. The platform enables advanced analytics, machine learning, and data science initiatives using cloud-native storage technologies. Data Hub consolidates data ingestion, storage, governance, and consumption layers with built-in data catalog, lineage tracking, and quality monitoring. It supports SQL queries, API access, BI tool integration, and ML/AI workloads, serving as the foundation for Temenos analytics and reporting capabilities.

components.name: Infinity/Digital
components.description: Temenos Infinity is a comprehensive digital banking platform that delivers customer experiences across web banking, mobile banking (iOS and Android), tablets, and wearables. Built with an API-first architecture, it supports digital onboarding, loan origination, and end-to-end customer journeys. Key features include Spotlight for personalized insights and recommendations, and Assist for AI-powered customer support. The platform offers a low-code extensibility framework enabling banks to customize digital journeys with minimal coding. Infinity supports headless deployment, allowing banks to use their own front-ends while leveraging its middleware orchestration capabilities. It integrates with Temenos Exchange for fintech partnerships and provides strong customer authentication (SCA) and multi-factor authentication (MFA) for PSD2 compliance. Infinity was rebranded to Temenos Digital in 2024.

components.name: Open Products
components.description: Open Products is a modular product architecture initiative introduced in 2023 that enables composable, API-first banking products. It allows banks to deploy standalone product modules that can operate independently or integrate with Transact core banking. Open Products supports microservices-based architecture with individual components for Lending, Deposits, Limits, and Pricing that can be assembled according to business needs. The approach enables faster product launches and best-of-breed integration strategies.

components.name: Holdings
components.description: Holdings is a core microservice in the Temenos MSF (Microservices Framework) that provides a unified view of customer financial positions across all banking products. Introduced in 2019, it aggregates account holdings, balances, and positions from Transact core banking through REST APIs. Holdings has evolved significantly through consolidation: the Arrangements microservice was merged into Holdings in 2024, and Balances and Activities was absorbed in 2025. In 2024, Holdings was enhanced to ingest payment transaction data to support the Payments Cockpit dashboard, enabling centralized payment visibility alongside account positions. Holdings implements the CQRS pattern for read-optimized queries and integrates with Data Event Streaming for event-driven updates.

components.name: Arrangements
components.description: Arrangements was a microservice that exposed Temenos Arrangement Architecture (AA) capabilities through modern REST APIs. Launched in 2019 alongside the Transact platform split, it provided lightweight access to AA product arrangements, contracts, and their lifecycle states without requiring direct T24 core integration. The service supported arrangement inquiries, property retrieval, and activity execution for deposit, lending, and account products. In 2024, Arrangements functionality was merged into the Holdings microservice as part of Temenos' microservices consolidation strategy, reducing service sprawl while maintaining API compatibility.

components.name: Balances and Activities
components.description: Balances and Activities was a specialized microservice introduced in 2022 to provide optimized access to account balance information and transaction activities. It offered high-performance balance lookups, real-time available balance calculations, and activity history retrieval through dedicated REST endpoints. The service was designed for digital channels requiring fast balance responses without the overhead of full arrangement queries. In 2025, Balances and Activities was retired and its functionality consolidated into the Holdings microservice, which now serves as the unified service for all customer position and activity data.

components.name: Marketing Catalogue
components.description: Marketing Catalogue was an MSF microservice launched in 2019 that exposed banking product definitions and eligibility rules through REST APIs. It provided digital channels with access to available products, their features, pricing tiers, and eligibility criteria without requiring direct Transact integration. The service supported product comparison, feature enumeration, and dynamic product recommendations based on customer profiles. In 2025, Marketing Catalogue was superseded by Product Manager (TPM), which offers enhanced product configuration capabilities, improved catalog management, and better integration with the composable banking architecture.

components.name: Product Manager (TPM)
components.description: Product Manager (TPM) is Temenos' modern microservice for comprehensive product configuration and catalog management. Introduced in 2022 as the successor to Marketing Catalogue, TPM provides advanced capabilities for defining banking products, managing product lifecycles, and configuring product bundles. It supports dynamic product assembly, pricing rules, eligibility criteria, and channel-specific product variants. TPM integrates with Arrangement Architecture for product instantiation and supports the composable banking paradigm where products can be assembled from modular components. The service exposes OpenAPI-compliant REST interfaces for product discovery and configuration.

components.name: Party
components.description: Party is a foundational microservice in the Temenos MSF that manages customer and counterparty data independent of core banking transactions. Introduced in 2019, it provides REST APIs for creating, retrieving, and updating party information including individuals, organizations, and their relationships. Party supports KYC data management, party roles, contact details, and identity documents. The microservice enables digital onboarding flows and integrates with Due Diligence services for compliance checks. Party functioned primarily as a query-only service or proxy to underlying core banking customer data, and is being enhanced by Party Master in 2026.

components.name: Party Master
components.description: Party Master is the next-generation customer information microservice that serves as the master CIF (Customer Information File) across the entire bank. It provides a single source of truth for customer data spanning both retail and corporate clients, consolidating party information that was previously fragmented across multiple systems. Party Master represents an evolution from the original Party microservice, which functioned primarily as a query-only service or proxy to underlying core banking customer data. With Party Master, banks gain full read-write capabilities for managing customer lifecycles, hierarchical corporate structures, beneficial ownership, and complex multi-entity relationships. The service supports real-time synchronization with downstream systems and provides comprehensive APIs for customer data management across all channels and applications.

components.name: Callback Registry
components.description: Callback Registry was an MSF microservice introduced in 2019 that managed webhook registrations and callback notifications for event-driven integrations. It allowed external systems to register callback URLs for specific business events, maintained subscription state, and orchestrated HTTP callbacks when events occurred in Transact. The service supported retry logic, delivery confirmation, and callback security through signature verification. Callback Registry was retired in 2024 as its functionality was largely superseded by the more comprehensive Event Framework, which provides native Kafka and message queue integration for event distribution.

components.name: Service Orchestrator
components.description: Service Orchestrator was an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 to coordinate complex multi-step banking processes across distributed services. It implemented workflow patterns for orchestrating API calls across Transact, other microservices, and external systems. The service managed transaction boundaries, compensation logic for failures, and provided visibility into process execution state. Service Orchestrator supported saga patterns for distributed transactions and long-running processes. In 2025, it was replaced by Event Store, which provides event-sourced orchestration with better scalability and integration with the Event Framework architecture.

components.name: Event Store
components.description: Event Store is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that provides event sourcing and event persistence capabilities for the Temenos architecture. It stores business events as an immutable log, enabling event replay, temporal queries, and audit trails. Event Store integrates with the Event Framework for event ingestion and distribution, supporting both business events and data events. The service enables event-driven microservices to reconstruct state from event history and supports complex event processing. In 2025, Event Store absorbed Service Orchestrator responsibilities, providing event-sourced workflow orchestration.

components.name: Origination Data
components.description: Origination Data is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that manages application data throughout the product origination lifecycle. It stores and retrieves application submissions, supporting documents, applicant information, and decision data for lending, account opening, and other origination processes. The service provides APIs for creating applications, updating application state, and retrieving application history. Origination Data integrates with Origination Processing for workflow execution and with Due Diligence for compliance verification. It supports document management, data validation, and maintains audit trails for regulatory compliance.

components.name: Origination Processing
components.description: Origination Processing is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that executes business workflows for product origination journeys. It orchestrates the sequence of activities in lending origination, account opening, and customer onboarding including credit checks, identity verification, document collection, and approval workflows. The service integrates with external decisioning systems, credit bureaus, and fraud detection services. Origination Processing supports configurable workflow definitions, parallel task execution, and handles both straight-through processing for simple applications and complex multi-stage approval processes.

components.name: Consent
components.description: Consent is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that manages customer consent records for data sharing, marketing communications, and regulatory compliance. It provides APIs for recording, retrieving, and revoking customer consents across different consent types and purposes. The service supports Open Banking consent management, GDPR data processing consents, and marketing opt-in/opt-out preferences. Consent maintains consent history with timestamps and audit trails, enabling banks to demonstrate regulatory compliance. It integrates with Party services for customer identification and with digital channels for consent collection workflows.

components.name: Billing Metering
components.description: Billing Metering was an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that tracked service usage and generated billing events for consumption-based pricing models. It provided metering APIs for recording API calls, transaction volumes, and feature utilization across Temenos services. The service supported usage aggregation, billing period management, and integration with invoicing systems. Billing Metering enabled banks to implement usage-based pricing for their own customers and supported Temenos SaaS consumption tracking. The service was retired in 2024 as billing functionality was consolidated into platform-level capabilities.

components.name: Campaign
components.description: Campaign is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that manages marketing campaigns, offers, and targeted customer communications. It provides APIs for creating campaign definitions, defining target segments, managing offer catalogs, and tracking campaign performance. Campaign supports next-best-action recommendations, personalized offers based on customer profiles, and campaign effectiveness analytics. The service integrates with digital channels for offer presentation, with Party for customer segmentation, and with Analytics for performance measurement. Campaign enables banks to execute omnichannel marketing strategies through centralized campaign management.

components.name: Savings Pot
components.description: Savings Pot is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that enables goal-based savings functionality for retail banking customers. It provides APIs for creating savings goals, setting target amounts and dates, configuring automatic transfers, and tracking progress toward financial objectives. Savings Pot supports multiple concurrent goals, round-up savings from transactions, and milestone notifications. The service integrates with Holdings for balance management and with digital channels for customer-facing savings interfaces. It enables banks to offer modern savings experiences that help customers achieve specific financial goals.

components.name: Account Aggregation
components.description: Account Aggregation is an MSF microservice that consolidates financial account information from multiple sources into unified customer views, supporting PSD2 open banking requirements. It enables customers to view external bank accounts alongside their Temenos-held accounts through integration with open banking aggregators like SaltEdge or direct bank connections. The service provides APIs for connecting external accounts, retrieving consolidated balances, and displaying cross-institution transaction history. Temenos expects banks to either manually integrate with third-party financial institutions or use an open banking aggregator service.

components.name: Due Diligence
components.description: Due Diligence is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that orchestrates customer due diligence processes for KYC, AML, and regulatory compliance. It provides APIs for initiating identity verification, screening against sanctions lists, performing risk assessments, and managing periodic reviews. Due Diligence integrates with external verification providers, identity document services, and watchlist screening databases. The service supports risk-based approaches where verification intensity matches customer risk profiles. It maintains compliance documentation, supports ongoing monitoring, and provides audit trails for regulatory examinations.

components.name: Generic Config
components.description: Generic Config is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that provides centralized configuration management for microservices and applications. It offers APIs for storing, retrieving, and managing configuration parameters including feature flags, runtime settings, and environment-specific values. Generic Config supports configuration versioning, hierarchical configuration inheritance, and dynamic configuration updates without service restarts. The service enables consistent configuration across distributed microservices and supports multi-tenant configurations. It integrates with deployment pipelines for configuration promotion across environments.

components.name: Receipts
components.description: Receipts is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that manages transaction receipt generation, storage, and retrieval. It provides APIs for creating digital receipts for banking transactions, storing receipt documents, and enabling customer access to transaction confirmations. Receipts supports multiple receipt formats including PDF, structured data, and email-ready formats. The service integrates with transaction processing to automatically generate receipts and with digital channels for receipt delivery. It maintains receipt archives for regulatory retention requirements and supports receipt regeneration from historical transactions.

components.name: Service Request
components.description: Service Request is an MSF microservice introduced in 2021 that manages customer service requests, inquiries, and case management workflows. It provides APIs for creating, tracking, and resolving service tickets including account inquiries, dispute handling, and general banking service requests. The microservice supports request categorization, priority assignment, SLA tracking, and integration with workflow engines for request routing. Service Request enables omnichannel service management where requests from any channel are tracked consistently. The service remains active and forms the foundation for the enhanced Service Request 2.0 capabilities.

components.name: Virtual Tables
components.description: Virtual Tables is an MSF integration service introduced in 2022 that provides data abstraction between microservices and underlying data sources. It creates virtual data views that aggregate data from Transact core banking, microservice databases, and external systems into unified queryable tables. Virtual Tables supports read-through data access without data replication, enabling real-time data consistency. The service integrates with MDAL (Microservices Data Abstraction Layer) and supports the Transact Explorer and Workbench development tools. It simplifies data access patterns for digital banking applications requiring cross-system data.

components.name: Service Request 2.0
components.description: Service Request 2.0 is an enhanced microservice introduced in 2023 that extends the original Service Request capabilities with advanced case management features. It provides improved workflow orchestration, intelligent request routing based on rules and machine learning, and enhanced integration with digital channels. Service Request 2.0 supports complex case hierarchies, multi-party involvement, automated escalation, and comprehensive audit trails. The service integrates with Temenos Journey Manager (TJM) for customer-facing request tracking and with analytics services for service quality insights and operational optimization.

components.name: CAMT
components.description: CAMT (Cash Management) is an ISO 20022-compliant microservice introduced in 2022 within the Temenos Payments Hub. It provides standardized bank-to-customer cash management messaging including account statements, balance reports, and transaction notifications. CAMT supports key ISO 20022 message types such as CAMT.052 for intraday account reports, CAMT.053 for end-of-day statements, and CAMT.054 for credit/debit notifications. The microservice enables corporate treasury systems and ERP platforms to receive structured transaction data in the universal ISO 20022 format, replacing legacy MT940/MT942 messages. CAMT integrates with Temenos Transact for account data and with the Payments Hub for transaction enrichment, supporting real-time and batch statement generation across multiple currencies and accounts.

components.name: Enterprise Pricing
components.description: Enterprise Pricing is a modular pricing engine introduced in 2022. It provides centralized, configurable pricing capabilities across all banking products, enabling banks to define complex pricing rules, tiered rates, and relationship-based discounts. The module supports real-time pricing calculations for deposits, lending, and fees, integrating with Arrangement Architecture for product-level pricing and with external market data sources. Enterprise Pricing enables dynamic pricing strategies based on customer segments, product bundles, and market conditions. It operates as a standalone module deployable via microservices architecture, supporting API-first integration patterns for omnichannel pricing consistency across digital and branch channels.

components.name: Market Data
components.description: Market Data is an integration module introduced in 2022 that provides Temenos Transact with real-time and historical financial market information. It serves as the conduit for external market data feeds including exchange rates, interest rate benchmarks, securities prices, and commodity values. The module integrates with major market data providers and internal treasury systems to support trading, treasury operations, and product pricing calculations. Market Data maintains reference rates used across Arrangement Architecture products for interest calculations, FX conversions, and valuations. It supports scheduled batch updates and real-time streaming, ensuring consistent market data across all banking operations and regulatory reporting requirements.

components.name: Reference Data
components.description: Reference Data is a foundational integration module introduced in 2022 that manages static and semi-static data entities across the Temenos banking platform. It centralizes management of currencies, countries, bank identifiers (BIC/SWIFT codes), regulatory codes, and industry classifications. The module provides a single source of truth for reference information consumed by core banking, payments, regulatory reporting, and digital channels. Reference Data supports versioning, effective dating, and audit trails for compliance requirements. It integrates with external reference data sources and regulatory bodies for automated updates, reducing manual maintenance and ensuring data consistency across multi-entity and multi-jurisdictional banking operations.

components.name: Deposits and Accounts
components.description: Deposits and Accounts is a banking module introduced in 2022 for modular core banking. It provides comprehensive functionality for current accounts, savings accounts, term deposits, and notice accounts, built on Arrangement Architecture foundations. The module handles account opening, balance management, interest accrual and capitalization, statement generation, and account servicing. It supports multi-currency accounts, pooled account structures, and sweep arrangements. Deposits and Accounts integrates with Enterprise Pricing for rate calculations, Party for customer management, and Holdings for consolidated balance views. The module is deployable as a cloud-native component with full API exposure for digital channel integration.

components.name: Lending
components.description: Lending is a comprehensive credit module introduced in 2023 for modular core banking. It manages the complete lending lifecycle including loan origination, disbursement, repayment schedules, interest calculations, and collections. The module supports diverse lending products: mortgages, personal loans, overdrafts, credit cards, and commercial facilities. Built on Arrangement Architecture, Lending provides configurable repayment schedules, flexible interest calculation methods, and automated fee processing. It integrates with Limits and Collateral for credit risk management, Enterprise Pricing for rate determination, and external credit bureaus for decisioning. The module supports Islamic finance structures and regulatory compliance for consumer lending across multiple jurisdictions.

components.name: Limits and Collateral
components.description: Limits and Collateral modules provide comprehensive risk management within Temenos Transact as microservices. The Limits module offers centralized real-time control over credit and market risk exposures, enabling limit definition at multiple hierarchical levels (individual customers, groups, countries, currencies). It performs real-time validation during transaction processing to prevent breaches and supports complex structures like joint limits, temporary limits, and time-banded limits. The Collateral module provides flexible management of internal and external collateral assets, supporting collateral pools, cross-pledging across multiple obligations, and granular asset-level rules for advance ratios and concentration caps. It ensures real-time collateral sufficiency calculations and maintains full auditability of allocations and valuations for regulatory compliance.

components.name: Unified Ledger
components.description: Unified Ledger is Temenos's next-generation enterprise ledger module designed to serve as a single source of truth for all balances, instruments, and movements across the entire bank. It is core and product agnostic, meaning it works across multiple banking systems without dependency on any specific core banking platform. The module enables progressive transformation by allowing banks to modernize incrementally without disrupting existing operations. Key capabilities include back-dated and future-dated cashflow projections, enterprise-level scalability with High Volume Transaction (HVT) support, and compatibility with distributed databases. Unified Ledger supports headless postings through GAI (Generic Accounting Interface), eliminating direct dependency on Transact's General Ledger. It is fully integrated with APIs and events for real-time data access and event-driven architectures, positioning it as a foundational component for banks pursuing composable banking strategies.

components.name: RPC via InfoBasic
components.description: RPC via InfoBasic (1985-1996) was Temenos's earliest integration mechanism, enabling remote procedure calls between external systems and the EBS/Globus core banking platform. Built on the InfoBasic programming language, it allowed external applications to invoke banking functions through direct procedure calls over a stateful Telnet connection. While functional for its era, this approach created tight coupling between systems and required maintaining persistent sessions. The method lacked standardization and scalability, making it unsuitable for growing integration needs. RPC via InfoBasic was superseded by the Open Financial Service (OFS) protocol in 1996, which introduced a more flexible, stateless messaging approach to external system integration.

components.name: OFS
components.description: OFS (Open Financial Service), introduced in 1996, is Temenos's foundational messaging protocol for external system integration. This text-based, stateless protocol enables request-response communication between external applications and the core banking system. OFS messages follow a structured format containing version, source, credentials, operation type, and field-value pairs. Supported operations include INPUT (create), AUTHORISE (approve), DELETE (remove), REVERSE (undo), and ENQUIRY (query). The protocol flows through an OFS Gateway to TOCF and into Transact Core, with parsing, validation, and transaction processing handled internally. Despite being nearly three decades old, OFS remains supported for backward compatibility and continues to underpin many integration patterns within the Temenos ecosystem.

components.name: JMS
components.description: JMS (Java Message Service) support was added to Temenos in 2009 as part of the enterprise integration expansion, enabling asynchronous messaging between T24/Transact and external systems through Java-based message queuing. JMS provides a standard API for message-oriented middleware, allowing banks to integrate with various JMS-compliant message brokers. This technology facilitates publish-subscribe and point-to-point messaging patterns, improving system decoupling and enabling scalable integration architectures. JMS support remains valuable for enterprise customers invested in Java middleware infrastructure, and continues to be supported alongside Kafka and IBM MQ as a messaging transport option within the Temenos integration ecosystem.

components.name: IBM MQ
components.description: IBM MQ integration was introduced in 2009 to support enterprise message queuing between T24/Transact and external systems. As a leading enterprise messaging platform, IBM MQ provides reliable, secure, and transactional message delivery across distributed systems. The Temenos integration enables both inbound and outbound message flows through MQ queues, supporting the Integration Framework and Event Framework architectures. Configuration involves connection factories, queue managers, and channels for establishing communication. IBM MQ remains actively supported in Temenos deployments, particularly in enterprise environments where IBM middleware is standard. It serves as one of the primary transport mechanisms for the Event Framework alongside Apache Kafka, handling Business Events and Data Events.

components.name: Oracle AQ
components.description: Oracle AQ (Advanced Queuing) support was added in 2009 to enable message-based integration for Temenos deployments using Oracle Database. Oracle AQ provides database-integrated queuing capabilities, allowing messages to participate in database transactions and leverage Oracle's reliability features. This integration was particularly valuable for banks running T24 on Oracle Database, as it eliminated the need for separate message queue infrastructure. Messages could be enqueued and dequeued as part of banking transactions, ensuring consistency between business operations and integration flows. Oracle AQ support was retired in 2016 as Temenos consolidated around more widely adopted messaging platforms and prepared for cloud-native architectures.

components.name: Sun One MQ
components.description: Sun One MQ (Sun Java System Message Queue) support was introduced in 2009 as part of Temenos's multi-vendor message queue strategy. This JMS-compliant message broker from Sun Microsystems enabled asynchronous integration between T24 and external systems for customers using Sun infrastructure. Sun One MQ provided reliable message delivery with features like persistent storage, transaction support, and clustering for high availability. The integration allowed banks to leverage existing Sun middleware investments while implementing enterprise integration patterns. Support for Sun One MQ was discontinued in 2011, coinciding with Oracle's acquisition of Sun Microsystems and the subsequent consolidation of messaging products, leading customers to migrate to alternative MQ solutions.

components.name: TAG
components.description: TAG (Temenos Application Gateway), introduced in 2007, provided application-level gateway services for T24 integration. TAG served as an intermediary layer that exposed T24 functionality to external systems through a more accessible interface than direct OFS messaging. It handled protocol translation, security enforcement, and request routing between external clients and the core banking system. TAG was particularly useful for web applications and third-party integrations that required simplified access to banking operations. The component supported various authentication mechanisms and provided logging and monitoring capabilities. TAG was retired in 2018 when the comprehensive API Framework was introduced, offering more modern REST-based APIs with OpenAPI specifications and enhanced security features.

components.name: TWS
components.description: TWS (Temenos Web Services), launched in 2008, exposed T24 banking functionality through SOAP-based web services. This technology enabled standards-based integration using WS-* protocols, making T24 accessible to enterprise service-oriented architectures (SOA). TWS provided WSDL definitions for banking operations, allowing clients to generate proxy code and invoke services programmatically. The web services layer handled XML serialization, security token processing, and transaction coordination. TWS was particularly important during the SOA era when SOAP web services were the dominant enterprise integration standard. The component was eventually superseded by IRIS R18 in 2021, as REST APIs with JSON payloads became the preferred integration approach over XML-based SOAP services.

components.name: IRIS 1.0
components.description: IRIS 1.0 (Interaction Framework), introduced in 2012, marked Temenos's first REST API layer for T24. This framework exposed banking functionality through RESTful endpoints supporting both JSON and XML formats, along with ODATA query capabilities. IRIS 1.0 handled HTTP method mapping (GET for read, POST for create, PUT for update, DELETE for remove), request routing, and response transformation. The architecture included REST and ODATA handlers, a resource manager, and a router directing requests to appropriate version handlers, enquiry handlers, or T24 services. IRIS 1.0 enabled modern web and mobile applications to integrate with T24 through standardized REST patterns, significantly improving developer experience compared to OFS messaging. It was upgraded to IRIS 2.0 in 2016.

components.name: IRIS 2.0
components.description: IRIS 2.0, released in 2016, enhanced Temenos's REST API capabilities with improved performance, security, and functionality. Building on IRIS 1.0's foundation, this version introduced better REST compliance, enhanced query capabilities, and improved error handling. IRIS 2.0 provided more efficient data serialization, reduced latency through optimizations, and expanded the range of banking operations exposed through APIs. The framework supported advanced filtering, pagination, and field selection for enquiry operations. Security improvements included better authentication integration and authorization controls. IRIS 2.0 served as a transitional technology, bridging the gap between IRIS 1.0's initial REST implementation and the comprehensive API Framework that would arrive in 2018 with full OpenAPI specification support.

components.name: API Framework
components.description: The API Framework, introduced in 2018, provides Temenos's comprehensive OpenAPI-based API management capability. Built on Apache Camel with REST-first design principles, it exposes Transact functionality through standardized REST APIs documented via Swagger. The framework implements multi-layer security including JWT authentication, OAuth 2.0 flows, and XACML authorization. API versioning follows semantic versioning with URL-based version paths. The architecture includes API specification layer, security layer, processing layer (routing, validation, transformation), and integration layer connecting to IRIS and OFS. Out-of-the-box APIs cover Holdings, Party, Product, Lending, Payments, and Reference data. Banks can create custom APIs using Workbench's API Designer. The framework supports rate limiting, pagination, caching, and comprehensive error handling.

components.name: IRIS R18
components.description: IRIS R18, introduced in 2018, represents the mature evolution of Temenos's Interaction Framework with full OpenAPI/Swagger specification support. This version integrates seamlessly with the API Framework, providing standardized REST APIs with semantic versioning and comprehensive documentation. IRIS R18 features enhanced security through JWT token authentication, OAuth 2.0 flows, and XACML-based authorization. The architecture supports API versioning, request validation, response transformation, and advanced error handling with structured error responses. IRIS R18 continues as an active component in the Transact ecosystem, serving as the foundational API layer that connects external consumers to core banking functionality through well-documented, standards-compliant REST endpoints.

components.name: Swagger/OpenAPI
components.description: Swagger/OpenAPI support, formalized in Temenos in 2018, provides standardized API documentation and specification capabilities for Transact APIs. OpenAPI Specification (formerly Swagger) defines REST APIs in a machine-readable format, enabling automatic documentation generation, client SDK creation, and API testing. Temenos APIs are documented through Swagger UI, providing interactive exploration of endpoints, parameters, request/response schemas, and authentication requirements. The specifications support semantic versioning, allowing clear API evolution management. OpenAPI integration enables banks to understand available APIs, generate client code in various languages, and integrate API documentation into their developer portals. This standard remains fundamental to Temenos's API-first strategy.

components.name: Integration Framework
components.description: The Integration Framework, introduced in 2011, provided MQ-based event generation for external system integration with T24. This framework enabled the core banking system to generate events when data changed, pushing notifications to external systems through message queues. It supported asynchronous communication patterns, decoupling T24 from consuming applications and enabling real-time integration without polling. The framework worked with various MQ providers including IBM MQ and Oracle AQ. Events were generated from Transact transactions and formatted for external consumption. The Integration Framework was superseded by the Event Framework in 2021, which expanded capabilities by combining MQ and Kafka transport options while introducing structured Business Events and Data Events.

components.name: ESB Adapter
components.description: ESB Adapter, introduced in 2012, provided pre-built connectivity between T24/Transact and enterprise service bus platforms. Temenos built specific adapters for Fiorano, Microsoft BizTalk, IBM Integration Bus (IIB), Oracle Service Bus (OSB), and MuleSoft. These adapters enabled integration through standardized message formats, routing, transformation, and protocol conversion. The adapters supported message flow orchestration, allowing complex integration scenarios involving multiple systems. ESB Adapters handled XML transformation, security integration, and monitoring for enterprise middleware platforms. This approach leveraged the bank's existing ESB investments while providing T24 connectivity. The ESB Adapter capability was phased out in 2021 as the Event Framework provided more modern event-driven integration patterns.

components.name: Biztalk
components.description: The Microsoft BizTalk adapter, available from 2012 to 2018, enabled integration between T24 and Microsoft's enterprise integration platform. This adapter allowed BizTalk Server to communicate with T24 through standardized messaging, supporting orchestrations, transformations, and business process automation. Banks using Microsoft middleware could leverage BizTalk's visual design tools to create integration workflows involving T24 banking operations. The adapter handled message format conversion between BizTalk's XML-based processing and T24's OFS messaging. BizTalk integration was discontinued in 2018 as Temenos consolidated integration approaches around the API Framework and modern REST-based patterns, moving away from heavyweight ESB-style integrations toward lighter-weight API-driven architectures.

components.name: Fiorano
components.description: The Fiorano ESB adapter, available from 2012 to 2018, provided integration between T24 and Fiorano's enterprise service bus platform. Fiorano SOA Platform offered distributed integration capabilities, and this adapter enabled banks using Fiorano to connect their middleware infrastructure with core banking operations. The adapter supported Fiorano's event-driven architecture, message routing, and transformation services. Integration patterns included publish-subscribe messaging, request-response operations, and file-based data exchange. Like other ESB adapters, Fiorano support was discontinued in 2018 as Temenos transitioned to API Framework-based integrations, reflecting the broader industry shift from ESB-centric to API-first integration architectures.

components.name: IIB
components.description: The IBM Integration Bus (IIB) adapter, available from 2017 to 2021, enabled connectivity between T24/Transact and IBM's integration middleware platform. IIB (formerly WebSphere Message Broker) provides enterprise message flow processing, transformation, and routing capabilities. The adapter allowed banks using IBM middleware to integrate Transact with their broader enterprise architecture through IIB's message flows and orchestrations. Integration supported various protocols, message formats, and transaction patterns native to the IBM middleware stack. The IIB adapter was retired in 2021 when the Event Framework provided more flexible integration options through Kafka and MQ, reducing the need for dedicated ESB adapter maintenance.

components.name: OSB
components.description: The Oracle Service Bus (OSB) adapter, available from 2017 to 2021, connected T24/Transact with Oracle's enterprise service bus platform. OSB provides service virtualization, message transformation, and intelligent routing for SOA-based architectures. Banks using Oracle middleware could leverage this adapter to expose T24 services through OSB, enabling centralized service governance and monitoring. The adapter supported OSB's proxy services, business services, and pipeline processing for message handling. Integration patterns included SOAP and REST service exposure, JMS messaging, and file-based transfers. OSB adapter support ended in 2021 as the Event Framework offered more modern integration approaches aligned with cloud-native architectures.

components.name: MuleESB
components.description: The MuleSoft ESB adapter, available from 2017 to 2021, provided integration between T24/Transact and the Mule runtime engine. MuleSoft's Anypoint Platform offers extensive connectivity to SaaS applications, databases, and enterprise systems. This adapter enabled banks using MuleSoft to incorporate Transact banking operations into their integration flows, supporting Mule's flow-based message processing and DataWeave transformations. The adapter worked with MuleSoft's connector ecosystem, allowing complex integration scenarios combining banking with CRM, ERP, and other enterprise systems. MuleESB adapter support was discontinued in 2021 as the Event Framework provided native event streaming capabilities that complemented rather than competed with integration platforms.

components.name: Inflow
components.description: Inflow, introduced in 2018, managed inbound integration processing for Temenos systems specifically through IBM MQ (Message Queue). This component handled message reception from external systems via MQ, providing message transformation, routing logic, and transaction orchestration for inbound requests. Inflow processed MQ messages, performed validation and transformation, then forwarded requests to IRIS and the core banking system for processing. The architecture supported queue-based asynchronous integration patterns commonly used in enterprise banking environments with IBM middleware. Inflow was consolidated into the Event Framework in 2021, which provided a more unified approach to both inbound and outbound integration with enhanced event-driven capabilities supporting both MQ and Kafka transports.

components.name: Commit Capture
components.description: Commit Capture, introduced in 2018, provides transaction commit capture capabilities for Temenos data streaming. This component intercepts database commits within Transact, capturing data changes at the moment they are persisted. Commit Capture serves as a foundational technology for real-time data streaming, enabling immediate event generation without polling or batch processing delays. The captured changes feed into Data Event Streaming (DES) and the Data Hub, supporting operational reporting, analytics, and external system synchronization. Commit Capture works at the database level, capturing both field-level changes and complete record states. This technology remains active in Transact deployments, providing the real-time data capture essential for modern event-driven architectures.

components.name: Kafka
components.description: Apache Kafka integration was introduced in 2019 as part of Temenos's cloud-native transformation, providing high-throughput event streaming capabilities. Kafka serves as a primary transport mechanism for the Event Framework, enabling real-time event distribution through a publish-subscribe architecture. The integration supports CloudEvents specification for standardized event formatting, Avro serialization through Schema Registry, and structured topic organization (e.g., temenos.transact.accounts.events). Kafka enables both Business Events (account opened, payment made) and Data Events (balance changed, status updated) to flow to subscribers including analytics systems, external platforms, and microservices. This technology replaced older JMS-based messaging and provides the scalability and fault tolerance required for modern cloud-native banking architectures.

components.name: Event Framework
components.description: The Event Framework, introduced in 2021, represents Temenos's modern event-driven architecture combining MQ and Kafka transport options. This framework unified integration patterns by introducing structured Business Events (account opened, payment made, customer onboarded) and Data Events (balance changed, status updated, field modified). Events follow the CloudEvents specification and flow from Transact through event brokers (Kafka/Azure Event Hub or MQ) to various subscribers including analytics systems, external platforms, and microservices. The Event Framework replaced the Integration Framework, providing greater flexibility in transport selection and more sophisticated event categorization. It supports both synchronous and asynchronous patterns, enabling loosely-coupled integrations essential for cloud-native banking architectures.

components.name: DES
components.description: DES (Data Event Streaming) is Temenos' real-time data streaming platform introduced in 2019. It captures transactional changes from Transact using Commit Capture and publishes them as Avro-serialized events to Apache Kafka, Azure Event Hub, or AWS Kinesis. DES enables downstream systems to receive near-real-time data updates for analytics, integration, and operational purposes. It supports multiple data stores (ODS, ADS, SDS) and integrates with Data Hub for comprehensive data management.

components.name: Microservices Outbox
components.description: Microservices Outbox implements the transactional outbox pattern for reliable event publishing from Temenos microservices. Introduced in 2019, it ensures atomicity between database transactions and event publication by first writing events to an outbox table within the same transaction, then asynchronously publishing them to the Event Framework. This pattern guarantees that events are never lost even if the message broker is temporarily unavailable, providing exactly-once delivery semantics. Microservices Outbox integrates with Kafka and MQ transports, supporting both Business Events and Data Events across the microservices ecosystem.

components.name: Microservices Inbox
components.description: Microservices Inbox provides reliable event consumption for Temenos microservices using the inbox pattern. Introduced in 2019, it ensures idempotent message processing by tracking received events in an inbox table before processing, preventing duplicate handling of the same event. The inbox pattern is essential for maintaining data consistency in distributed systems where network failures or retries may cause duplicate message delivery. Microservices Inbox integrates with the Event Framework, supporting consumption from Kafka topics and MQ queues while providing deduplication, ordering guarantees, and dead-letter handling for failed events.

components.name: Outbox
components.description: Outbox, introduced in 2024, implements the transactional outbox pattern for reliable event publishing in Temenos systems. This component ensures that database transactions and event publications are atomic, preventing scenarios where data is committed but events fail to publish (or vice versa). The Outbox pattern writes events to a database table within the same transaction as business data changes, then a separate process reads from this outbox table and publishes events to the Event Framework. This approach guarantees exactly-once event delivery semantics and maintains data consistency between the core banking system and event consumers. Outbox replaces DES as the primary mechanism for event publishing.

components.name: Inbox
components.description: Inbox is the counterpart to the Outbox pattern, providing reliable inbound event consumption for Temenos Transact core banking. Planned for 2026, it implements idempotent message processing by tracking received events before processing, ensuring exactly-once semantics even when events are delivered multiple times due to network issues or retries. Inbox stores incoming events in a database table within the receiving transaction, enabling atomic consumption and processing. This pattern is essential for maintaining consistency when Transact receives events from external systems, microservices, or partner integrations through the Event Framework.

components.name: MDAL
components.description: MDAL (Master Data Access Layer), introduced in 2022, facilitates efficient data retrieval and management across distributed systems within the Temenos modular architecture. It provides a structured and flexible approach to accessing external data sources, enabling seamless integration within larger banking applications. MDAL is composed of Data Access Components (modular units encapsulating data access operations), Request Registry (API gateway for mapping requests), and Master Data Access Handler (configurable in Embedded, Inline, or Pre-composed modes). MDAL integrates smoothly with microservices architecture, treating each Data Access Component as a potential microservice for independent deployment and scaling.

components.name: IRIS
components.description: IRIS (Interaction Framework) was Temenos's REST API layer introduced in 2012, providing RESTful access to T24 banking functionality. IRIS 1.0 (2012) introduced REST and ODATA APIs with basic CRUD operations for T24 entities. IRIS 2.0 (2016) enhanced performance and added improved REST capabilities. IRIS R18 (2018) integrated OpenAPI specifications and versioning support. The framework exposed T24 business operations through standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), enabling web and mobile applications like TCIB and TCMB to interact with core banking services. IRIS was superseded by the API Framework in 2018, which provided a more comprehensive API-first architecture with enhanced OpenAPI integration and semantic versioning.

components.name: Adapter
components.description: The Adapter microservice, introduced in 2021, provides the connectivity layer between Transact core banking and the Event Framework. Built on Apache Camel, this adapter enables events generated within Transact to be published to external event brokers, bridging the core banking execution environment with modern messaging infrastructure. The Adapter handles event serialization, routing configuration, protocol translation, and delivery guarantees, ensuring reliable event transmission from core banking transactions to Kafka, Azure Event Hub, or MQ destinations. It supports both Business Events and Data Events, providing message transformation and the technical bridge that enables Transact to participate fully in event-driven architectures.

components.name: Exchange
components.description: Exchange, introduced in 2022, serves as Temenos's partner vendor exchange and marketplace for third-party integrations. This component provides a curated catalog of pre-built connectors, adapters, and integrations from Temenos partners, enabling banks to extend Transact functionality with specialized solutions. Exchange facilitates rapid integration with fintech providers, payment networks, regulatory services, and other banking ecosystem participants. The platform includes standardized integration patterns, documentation, and potentially pre-certified solutions that reduce implementation time and risk. Exchange represents Temenos's approach to ecosystem-based banking, allowing financial institutions to compose best-of-breed solutions while maintaining Transact as the core banking foundation.

components.name: DW.EXPORT
components.description: DW.EXPORT (Data Warehouse Export) is Temenos' batch data extraction utility introduced in 2009. It extracts data from the core banking system into external data warehouses for reporting and analytics purposes. DW.EXPORT supports scheduled extractions with configurable table selections, transforming T24/Transact's multi-value data structures into relational format suitable for business intelligence tools. The component remains active and serves as a foundational data extraction mechanism for banks requiring periodic batch data exports to downstream analytics systems.

components.name: BI Datamart
components.description: BI Datamart was a short-lived data mart solution introduced in 2014 and retired in 2015 when superseded by Data ExStore. It provided pre-structured data models optimized for business intelligence reporting, extracting and transforming T24 data into dimensional schemas suitable for BI tools. BI Datamart offered faster query performance for analytical workloads by pre-aggregating and denormalizing operational data. Its capabilities were absorbed into the more comprehensive Data ExStore component.

components.name: Data Framework
components.description: Data Framework was Temenos' unified data management architecture introduced in 2014 and retired in 2023 when replaced by Data Hub. It established the foundational patterns for extracting, transforming, and loading T24 data into analytical stores. Data Framework coordinated multiple data components including ExStore, streaming capabilities, and batch exports. It provided governance, metadata management, and data quality features that supported regulatory reporting and analytics use cases across the T24 platform era.

components.name: Data ExStore
components.description: Data ExStore (External Store) was introduced in 2015 as an enhanced data mart capability, replacing BI Datamart. It provided real-time and near-real-time data replication from T24 to external relational databases optimized for reporting and analytics. Data ExStore supported multiple target databases and offered configurable data transformation rules. The component was retired in 2023 when its capabilities were consolidated into the unified Data Hub platform for streamlined data management.

components.name: TDE
components.description: TDE (Temenos Data Engineering) is an in-memory data processing application built on Apache Spark, introduced in 2019 within the Temenos Data Hub ecosystem. It manages, processes, cleanses, and loads data into downstream databases. TDE oversees configuration and execution of both streaming jobs and custom data pipelines, supporting real-time and batch data delivery. It features a no-code drag-and-drop web interface for designing data workflows. TDE includes Administrator Module (configuration, monitoring, security), Designer Module (custom pipeline creation), and Scheduler Module (automated task execution). It ensures data quality, manages metadata governance, supports GDPR compliance, and enables event delivery to streaming platforms.

components.name: ODS
components.description: ODS (Operational Data Store) replicates data from Temenos Transact in near real-time and processes it to ensure data quality. Introduced in 2019 as part of Temenos Data Hub, it parses, cleanses, and stores data in a relational format (third normal form), making it ready for APIs, reporting, and analytics. ODS provides a structured, normalized view of transactional data, supporting both operational and analytical needs with real-time access to clean and consistent data. ODS APIs offer operational data optimized for customer service, transaction lookup, and real-time business monitoring without impacting core system performance.

components.name: ADS
components.description: ADS (Analytics Data Store) is a near-real-time analytics data store introduced in 2019 as part of the Temenos Data Hub architecture. It provides banking-specific analytical data from intra-day and historical perspectives, allowing for comprehensive analysis. ADS APIs are optimized to support trend analysis, data visualization, and BI tool integration. The store supports dashboards, historical reporting, and regulatory analytics, integrating with enterprise BI tools like Power BI, Tableau, and Qlik for comprehensive banking analytics and insights.

components.name: SDS
components.description: SDS (Snapshot Data Store) replicates both near real-time and historical data from Temenos Transact, introduced in 2019 as part of Temenos Data Hub. Like ODS, it parses, cleanses, and stores data in relational format but additionally provides end-of-day snapshots of financial data such as account balances, accrued interest, and effective interest rates. This snapshot capability is critical for historical reporting, regulatory compliance, and providing a historical view of financial data over time. SDS is ideal for feeding downstream systems such as risk management, treasury, and marketing.

components.name: Data Lake
components.description: Data Lake was Temenos' enterprise data lake solution introduced in 2019 and retired in 2023 when consolidated into Data Hub. It provided a centralized repository for storing raw, processed, and curated banking data at scale using cloud-native storage technologies. Data Lake supported both structured and semi-structured data, enabling advanced analytics, machine learning, and data science initiatives. Its capabilities were absorbed into the more comprehensive Data Hub architecture.

components.name: Data Hub
components.description: Data Hub is Temenos' unified data platform introduced in 2023, consolidating Data Lake, Data Framework, and Data ExStore capabilities. It provides a comprehensive data management solution with ingestion, storage, governance, and consumption layers. Data Hub supports raw, processed, and curated data zones with built-in data catalog, lineage tracking, and quality monitoring. It enables SQL queries, API access, BI tool integration, and ML/AI workloads on banking data.

components.name: Insight
components.description: Insight was Temenos' business intelligence and analytics platform introduced in 2009 and retired in 2019 when replaced by the Analytics platform. It provided pre-built dashboards, reports, and analytical capabilities for banking operations including customer analytics, product performance, and risk monitoring. Insight integrated directly with T24 data structures and offered drill-down capabilities for operational and strategic decision-making. The platform served banks' reporting needs during the T24 era before the transition to modern streaming-based analytics approaches.

components.name: Embedded Analytics
components.description: Embedded Analytics was a capability introduced in 2016 and retired in 2019 that provided in-application analytical visualizations directly within T24 user interfaces. It enabled real-time dashboards, charts, and KPIs to be displayed alongside operational screens without switching to separate BI tools. Embedded Analytics leveraged T24 data through optimized queries, offering contextual insights for customer service representatives, relationship managers, and operations staff during their daily workflows.

components.name: Analytics
components.description: Analytics is Temenos' advanced analytics platform introduced in 2017, replacing the earlier Insight solution. It provides comprehensive business intelligence capabilities including pre-built dashboards, custom report builders, and predictive analytics.
