Analytics integrates with DES and Data Hub for real-time and historical data analysis, supporting regulatory reporting, customer insights, risk monitoring, and operational metrics across the Transact and Infinity platforms.

components.name: Searchable DB (Lucene)
components.description: Searchable DB powered by Apache Lucene was introduced in 2017 and retired in 2019. It provided full-text search capabilities across T24 data, enabling users to quickly locate customers, accounts, and transactions using natural language queries. The Lucene-based implementation indexed key banking entities and supported faceted search, fuzzy matching, and relevance ranking. Its search capabilities were later incorporated into the SDS (Snapshot Data Store) component within the broader DES architecture.

components.name: Relational Replication
components.description: Relational Replication was a data replication capability introduced in 2018 and retired in 2019. It provided real-time replication of Transact data to external relational databases, transforming the multi-value data model into normalized relational schemas. Relational Replication supported multiple target databases and offered configurable mapping rules. Its functionality was absorbed into the broader DES architecture with TDE handling schema transformations.

components.name: XAI
components.description: XAI (Explainable AI) is an artificial intelligence capability introduced in 2019 that provides transparent, interpretable machine learning for banking decisions. It enables banks to understand and explain AI-driven recommendations for credit scoring, fraud detection, and customer insights. XAI supports regulatory requirements for algorithmic transparency, providing audit trails and explanations for model predictions that can be presented to customers and regulators.

components.name: InfoBasic
components.description: InfoBasic is Temenos's proprietary programming language, derived from BASIC syntax, introduced in 1985 with the original EBS system. It serves as the primary language for writing custom business logic, validation routines, and integration hooks within T24/Transact. InfoBasic code is compiled and executed through the TAFJ runtime (since 2011), which transpiles it to Java bytecode for platform-independent execution. The language features built-in database integration, string manipulation, and file operations, enabling developers to extend core banking functionality without modifying standard product code.

components.name: DevStudio
components.description: DevStudio, also known as Toolbox, was the first integrated development environment for T24, introduced in 2004. This Windows-only application provided essential development capabilities including an InfoBasic code editor, Version screen designer, Enquiry designer, and record browser with basic debugging support. DevStudio enabled developers to create and modify T24 customizations through a graphical interface rather than command-line tools. However, its limitations in version control, collaboration features, and cross-platform support led to its replacement by the Eclipse-based Design Studio in 2013.

components.name: AA Designer
components.description: AA Designer is a specialized visual design tool for configuring Arrangement Architecture products, introduced in 2009 alongside the revolutionary AA framework. It enables business analysts and developers to define product hierarchies, component compositions, property inheritances, and negotiable parameters without writing code. Through AA Designer, users create product groups, configure interest calculations, define statement frequencies, and establish eligibility rules. The tool generates the underlying AA configuration data, making complex product creation accessible while ensuring consistency with AA's component-based architecture.

components.name: T24 Updater
components.description: T24 Updater is a system update tool introduced in 2009 for applying patches, releases, and customization packages to T24/Transact environments. It manages the deployment of new versions, hotfixes, and local developments while handling dependency resolution and version compatibility checks. T24 Updater tracks installed components, validates package integrity, and provides rollback capabilities for failed deployments. The tool ensures controlled updates to production systems by managing the sequence of database changes, routine compilations, and configuration updates required for successful deployments.

components.name: Design Studio
components.description: Design Studio is the Eclipse-based integrated development environment introduced in 2013, replacing DevStudio. It provides a comprehensive suite of visual designers including Data Model Designer, InfoBasic Editor with syntax highlighting and code completion, Version Designer, Enquiry Designer, AA Designer, and PW Designer. Design Studio supports version control integration (SVN/Git), debugging capabilities, and plugin architecture for extensibility. The platform enables collaborative development with project management, dependency tracking, and integrated packaging through DS Packager. It remains actively used alongside the newer Workbench.

components.name: PW Designer
components.description: PW Designer was the Process Workflow visual design tool introduced in 2013 as part of Design Studio, retired in 2024. It enabled creation of business process workflows including approval chains, task routing, exception handling, and SLA monitoring configurations. Through a graphical interface, designers defined workflow stages, transition conditions, role assignments, and escalation rules. PW Designer generated the underlying Process Workflow definitions used by T24/Transact to automate business processes such as loan approvals, account openings, and customer service requests, reducing manual intervention and ensuring consistent processing.

components.name: Data Model Designer
components.description: Data Model Designer is a visual tool within Design Studio for defining and modifying T24/Transact data structures. Introduced in 2013, it enables developers to create custom tables, define field properties, establish multi-value associations, and configure validation rules through a graphical interface. The tool handles the complexity of T24's MultiValue data model, supporting primary keys, associated fields, and nested data structures. Data Model Designer generates the underlying data dictionary entries and ensures structural integrity across related tables and enquiries.

components.name: Integration Framework Designer
components.description: Integration Framework Designer is a Design Studio-based utility introduced in 2013 for building and configuring Integration Framework events. It provides a graphical interface within Design Studio for defining outbound event configurations that trigger when T24/Transact data changes. Developers use this tool to specify event definitions, configure message payloads, set filtering conditions, and define MQ destination queues for the Integration Framework. With the evolution to the Event Framework in 2021, the designer was enhanced to support both Business Events and Data Events, enabling configuration of Kafka topics alongside MQ queues and defining CloudEvents-compliant message structures for modern event-driven integration patterns.

components.name: Web Designer
components.description: Web Designer is a tool introduced in 2018 for creating web-based user interfaces for T24/Transact applications. It enables developers to design responsive web screens, configure widget layouts, and create custom user experiences without deep frontend development expertise. Web Designer integrates with the UXP (User Experience Platform) framework, generating HTML5/JavaScript interfaces that communicate with Transact through the API Framework. The tool supports theme customization, accessibility compliance, and mobile-responsive design patterns.

components.name: Java API
components.description: Java API is a development interface introduced in 2018 that enables direct Java programming integration with T24/Transact. It provides a programmatic interface for extending Transact functionality using standard Java code rather than InfoBasic, supporting developers familiar with Java ecosystems. The Java API integrates with TAFJ runtime, allowing custom Java classes to interact with Transact data, invoke business operations, and participate in transaction processing. This enables use of Java libraries, frameworks, and development tools for Transact customizations.

components.name: API Designer
components.description: API Designer is a tool introduced in 2018 for creating and managing REST APIs within the Temenos API Framework. It enables developers to define OpenAPI/Swagger specifications, configure API endpoints, establish authentication requirements, and map operations to underlying Transact functions. API Designer generates API documentation, validates request/response schemas, and supports versioning strategies. The tool accelerates API development by providing visual design capabilities while ensuring compliance with RESTful design principles and banking industry API standards. API Designer was embedded into Temenos Workbench in 2023 and continues as a major component within the unified development environment.

components.name: Workbench
components.description: Workbench is the next-generation web-based development environment introduced in 2020, complementing Design Studio. It provides a modern browser-based IDE with Data Model designer, Virtual Tables, Enquiry designer, Adapters, Version designer, Python Scripts support, Event Designer, and Java API integration. Workbench features native Git integration for version control, Karate testing framework for API testing, and cloud-native design principles. It supports collaborative development workflows, CI/CD pipeline integration, and runs entirely in the browser without local installation requirements.

components.name: GIT
components.description: GIT integration was formally added to Temenos development tools in 2022 within Workbench, providing native version control capabilities. It enables developers to use standard Git workflows including branching, merging, pull requests, and code reviews for Transact customizations. GIT integration supports GitOps practices, connecting development environments to repositories for continuous integration. This replaced earlier SVN-based version control, aligning Temenos development with modern software engineering practices and enabling collaboration through platforms like GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps.

components.name: Karate
components.description: Karate is the API testing framework integrated into Workbench in 2022, enabling automated testing of Transact REST APIs. Based on the open-source Karate framework, it uses Gherkin-like syntax for writing readable test scenarios that validate API responses, authentication flows, and business logic. Karate tests can verify status codes, response structures, and data values while supporting parameterized testing and environment-specific configurations. The framework integrates with CI/CD pipelines, enabling automated regression testing and quality assurance for API customizations.

components.name: Python Scripts
components.description: Python Scripts support was introduced in Workbench in 2022, enabling developers to write extensibility logic using Python alongside traditional InfoBasic. This addition brings Python's extensive library ecosystem, data processing capabilities, and machine learning frameworks to Transact development. Python scripts can perform custom calculations, data transformations, external service integrations, and analytics processing. The feature expands developer options beyond InfoBasic, attracting Python-skilled developers and enabling modern programming patterns within the Transact ecosystem.

components.name: DL.DEFINE
components.description: DL.DEFINE was the data dictionary definition tool used from 1994 to 2004 during the Globus era. It provided a command-line interface for defining and modifying T24 data structures, including tables, fields, and their relationships. Developers used DL.DEFINE to create metadata definitions that controlled data validation, field types, and multi-value associations. The tool was essential for customizing the MultiValue data model but required significant manual effort. It was replaced by BCON packager in 2004, which introduced more automated build and packaging capabilities.

components.name: BCON packager
components.description: BCON packager was the build and packaging tool for T24 customizations from 2004 to 2015. It replaced DL.DEFINE by introducing automated compilation, dependency management, and deployment package creation. BCON packager assembled InfoBasic routines, Version definitions, Enquiries, and data model changes into deployable packages for T24 environments. The tool streamlined the release management process but lacked integration with modern version control systems and IDE workflows. It was superseded by DS Packager in 2015, which integrated directly with Design Studio.

components.name: DS Packager
components.description: DS Packager is the Design Studio packaging tool introduced in 2015, replacing BCON packager. It provides integrated packaging capabilities directly within the Eclipse-based IDE, creating deployment packages from Design Studio projects. DS Packager handles dependency management, version control integration, and automated build processes. It assembles data models, routines, versions, enquiries, and configurations into deployable artifacts with manifest files describing contents and dependencies. The tool supports both local development and CI/CD pipeline integration for automated builds.

components.name: DSF Packager
components.description: DSF Packager (Design Studio Foundation Packager) was introduced in 2020 as an enhanced packaging tool for the cloud-native era. It extends DS Packager capabilities with declarative YAML-based package manifests, Git-native versioning, and CI/CD pipeline integration. DSF Packager supports dependency resolution across multiple package repositories, semantic versioning, and automated deployment validation. It aligns with modern DevOps practices, enabling infrastructure-as-code approaches to T24/Transact customization deployment across containerized and SaaS environments.

components.name: Prime Computer
components.description: Prime Computer was the original hardware platform for Temenos EBS (Electronic Banking System) from 1983 to 1990. It ran PRIMEOS operating system with Pick Information database, providing the foundational infrastructure for the first Temenos core banking deployments. Prime systems used proprietary 50-series processors with time-sharing capabilities supporting multiple concurrent users through terminal connections. The hardware imposed significant constraints on system scalability and geographic reach. As banking technology evolved, the dependency on Prime hardware became a limitation, driving the transition to hardware-agnostic Unix platforms that enabled Globus to run on diverse commodity hardware starting in 1990.

components.name: PRIMEOS
components.description: PRIMEOS was Prime Computer's proprietary operating system that ran on Prime hardware from 1983 to 1990. It provided the execution environment for the original EBS core banking system, managing process scheduling, memory allocation, and terminal I/O for Pick Information database operations. PRIMEOS supported multi-user time-sharing with character-based terminal access. The operating system was tightly coupled with Prime hardware architecture, creating a dependency that limited Temenos's ability to scale and diversify deployments. The transition to Unix in 1990 freed Temenos from this proprietary platform, enabling hardware independence that became a key competitive advantage during the Globus era.

components.name: JBase
components.description: JBase is a MultiValue database platform introduced in 2000 that provided platform independence for Globus deployments. It offered MultiValue compatibility while running on Windows, Unix, Linux, and various enterprise platforms, eliminating hardware dependencies. JBase delivered improved performance through modern database architecture while maintaining InfoBasic code compatibility. The platform supported concurrent processing, transaction management, and data replication for high-availability configurations. JBase remains an option for Transact deployments, particularly for banks with established MultiValue expertise, though TAFJ with RDBMS became the strategic platform direction starting in 2011.

components.name: DC Driver
components.description: DC Driver (Direct Connect Driver) was the database connectivity component introduced in 2004 alongside T24's RDBMS support. It provided the interface between the TAFC C-based runtime and Oracle RDBMS, enabling T24 to operate on relational databases rather than just MultiValue systems. The DC Driver handled connection management, query execution, and transaction coordination for T24 database operations. It abstracted database-specific operations, enabling T24 to work with different database vendors through a consistent interface. As TAFJ adoption increased with its native JDBC connectivity, DC Driver usage declined. The component was deprecated in 2020 in favor of JDBC drivers for all database access.

components.name: jdbc Driver
components.description: The JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) Driver became the standard database access mechanism for Temenos with the introduction of TAFJ in 2011. It provides database-agnostic connectivity supporting Oracle, DB2, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, NuoDB, and other RDBMS platforms through their respective JDBC implementations. The JDBC layer enables connection pooling, query optimization, and transaction management within the TAFJ runtime. This approach eliminated dependency on proprietary database drivers and MultiValue databases, enabling deployment on any JDBC-compliant database. Configuration includes pool sizing, validation queries, and timeout settings for optimal performance in banking workloads with high transaction volumes.

components.name: Pick Information
components.description: Pick Information was the MultiValue database system underlying EBS and early Globus from 1985 to 2000. Named after inventor Dick Pick, it stored data in nested, multi-valued records rather than flat relational tables, enabling flexible data modeling well-suited to banking's complex structures. Pick databases stored data in 'files' containing 'items' with 'attributes' that could contain multiple values and sub-values. This model efficiently represented hierarchical banking data but required specialized query approaches. Pick was replaced by Universe database starting in 1987, which maintained MultiValue compatibility while offering improved performance and platform support.

components.name: Universe
components.description: Universe was a MultiValue database platform adopted by Temenos in 1990 as an alternative to Pick Information, providing improved performance and broader platform support. Universe maintained compatibility with Pick's multi-value data model while running on Unix systems. It offered enhanced query capabilities, better concurrency handling, and improved scalability compared to its predecessor. Universe was the primary database for Globus deployments during the 1990s. The platform was phased out in 2000 when TAFC introduced support for JBase and relational databases, though Universe provided a stable foundation for many Globus deployments during its operational period.

components.name: Oracle DB
components.description: Oracle Database has been supported since 2004, representing the first RDBMS option for T24. It remains a primary enterprise database choice offering advanced features including Real Application Clusters (RAC) for high availability, partitioning for large data volumes, and advanced security options. Oracle integration utilizes JDBC connectivity through TAFJ with optimized query handling for banking workloads. The database supports both on-premises deployment and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) managed services. Oracle versions 12c, 19c, and 21c are certified, providing options for customers in Oracle-centric environments requiring enterprise database capabilities.

components.name: DB2
components.description: IBM DB2 has been supported since 2005, providing an RDBMS option for IBM ecosystem customers. It offers strong z/OS mainframe integration for banks with existing IBM infrastructure and supports both distributed and mainframe deployments. DB2 provides advanced features including BLU Acceleration for analytics, pureScale for scalability, and HADR for high availability. The database integrates via JDBC with TAFJ and supports deployment on AIX, Linux, and z/OS platforms. DB2 versions 10.5, 11.1, and 11.5 are certified, making it the strategic choice for organizations committed to IBM technology stacks.

components.name: SQL Server
components.description: Microsoft SQL Server has been supported since 2007, enabling T24/Transact deployment on Microsoft infrastructure. It provides integration with Windows Server, Active Directory, and Azure cloud services for Microsoft-centric organizations. SQL Server offers Always On availability groups for high availability, columnstore indexes for analytics, and Azure SQL Database for cloud deployment. The database supports JDBC connectivity with TAFJ and integrates with Azure services including Azure Synapse for analytics. SQL Server versions 2016, 2019, and 2022 are certified, providing a familiar platform for banks with Windows-based infrastructure.

components.name: NuoDB
components.description: NuoDB has been supported since 2019 as a distributed SQL database designed for cloud-native deployments. It provides elastic scaling, active-active multi-data-center deployment, and SQL compatibility with automatic data distribution. NuoDB enables horizontal scaling of database capacity without application changes, supporting variable banking workloads. The database maintains ACID compliance while distributing data across nodes, combining relational capabilities with cloud-native elasticity. NuoDB became relevant for banks requiring multi-cloud deployments or active-active disaster recovery configurations where traditional RDBMS replication presents challenges.

components.name: CosmosDB
components.description: Azure Cosmos DB support was introduced in 2020 as part of multi-cloud database exploration efforts. Cosmos DB offered global distribution, automatic scaling, and multiple consistency models (strong to eventual) that aligned with distributed banking deployments across geographic regions. The integration explored using Cosmos DB's SQL API for specific microservices workloads requiring low-latency global access, particularly for reference data and customer profile caching. However, the initiative was discontinued in 2022 as the cost model and data modeling constraints proved challenging for core banking transaction patterns. Temenos consolidated on proven RDBMS options (PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle) and specialized distributed databases (NuoDB) that better matched banking workload characteristics.

components.name: DynamoDB
components.description: AWS DynamoDB support was introduced in 2020 during cloud-native platform expansion to leverage Amazon's fully managed NoSQL database service. DynamoDB offered serverless scaling, single-digit millisecond performance, and tight integration with AWS services like Lambda and API Gateway. The integration targeted microservices requiring key-value or document storage patterns with predictable performance at scale. Use cases included session management, event logging, and caching layers for Transact microservices deployed on EKS/Fargate. However, like Cosmos DB, DynamoDB support was discontinued in 2022 as the NoSQL data model limitations and vendor lock-in concerns led to focus on portable database solutions that could operate across multiple cloud providers.

components.name: MySQL
components.description: MySQL has been supported since 2020 as a cost-effective open-source RDBMS option. It provides familiar SQL capabilities with broad cloud availability through Amazon RDS, Azure Database for MySQL, and Google Cloud SQL. MySQL offers replication, InnoDB storage engine with ACID compliance, and widespread community support. The database integrates via JDBC connector with TAFJ, supporting both community and enterprise editions. MySQL 8.0 is certified for Transact deployments, providing an entry-level database option for smaller deployments or development environments where licensing costs are significant considerations.

components.name: MongoDB
components.description: MongoDB has been supported since 2020 as a NoSQL document database option for specific use cases. It provides flexible schema design, horizontal scaling through sharding, and JSON-native document storage. MongoDB suits scenarios requiring flexible data models, such as customer preference storage, document management, or integration with applications generating unstructured data. The database is available as MongoDB Atlas managed service across cloud providers. While not typically used as the primary Transact database, MongoDB serves complementary roles in modern architectures where document storage enhances microservices or channel applications.

components.name: PostgreSQL
components.description: PostgreSQL has been supported since 2019, representing the cloud-native open-source database option. It offers cost-effective deployment without licensing fees while providing enterprise features including JSONB for flexible data, robust replication, and strong ACID compliance. PostgreSQL is available as managed services across all major clouds (Amazon RDS, Azure Database, Cloud SQL), simplifying operations. The database integrates via JDBC with TAFJ and supports advanced features like logical replication and point-in-time recovery. PostgreSQL became increasingly popular for cloud-native deployments where licensing costs and cloud portability are priorities.

components.name: Yugabyte
components.description: YugabyteDB support was introduced in 2021 as a distributed SQL database alternative to NuoDB. Yugabyte offered PostgreSQL compatibility with distributed architecture, enabling horizontal scaling while maintaining familiar SQL interfaces and ACID transactions. It provided multi-region deployment with synchronous replication, automatic sharding, and built-in resilience against zone failures. The PostgreSQL wire protocol compatibility simplified application integration since existing JDBC connections worked without modification. YugabyteDB targeted banks requiring cloud-native distributed databases with PostgreSQL ecosystem tool compatibility. Support was discontinued in 2025 as the market consolidated around established options (PostgreSQL, NuoDB) with stronger support ecosystems for banking workloads.

components.name: Redis
components.description: Redis integration was introduced in 2024 as an in-memory data store for high-performance caching and session management in Transact microservices deployments. Redis provides sub-millisecond response times for frequently accessed data, reducing database load and improving API response latency. Use cases include authentication token caching, API rate limiting, distributed session storage across Kubernetes pods, and reference data caching for customer and product information. Redis supports cluster mode for high availability and horizontal scaling across cloud providers through managed services (Amazon ElastiCache, Azure Cache for Redis, Google Memorystore). The component enhances microservices performance where persistent database access introduces unacceptable latency.

components.name: Oracle AS
components.description: Oracle Application Server was supported from 2009 to 2016 as a JEE deployment platform for T24 in Oracle-centric environments. It provided integration with Oracle database, Oracle Identity Management, and Oracle middleware products including Oracle Service Bus. The application server supported TOCF connectivity for T24 deployment with features including clustering, connection pooling, and Oracle-specific optimizations. Oracle AS was certified for deployments requiring tight integration with Oracle infrastructure and enterprise management tools. The platform was discontinued in 2016 as Oracle transitioned focus to WebLogic Server, which became the strategic Oracle JEE platform. Banks on Oracle AS migrated to WebLogic or alternative application servers.

components.name: WebSphere
components.description: IBM WebSphere Application Server has been supported since 2009 as a JEE application server platform. It provides enterprise deployment capabilities including clustering, workload management, and integration with IBM middleware ecosystem. WebSphere integrates with TOCF for T24/Transact connectivity and supports deployment on AIX, Linux, and Windows. The server offers advanced features including intelligent caching, web services support, and extensive monitoring capabilities. WebSphere versions 8.5 and 9.0 remain certified, serving banks with established IBM infrastructure and support agreements requiring enterprise JEE capabilities.

components.name: WebLogic
components.description: Oracle WebLogic Server has been supported since 2009 as an enterprise JEE application server. It provides robust clustering, advanced caching, and deep integration with Oracle database and middleware products. WebLogic integrates with TOCF for Transact connectivity and supports deployment on Linux, Solaris, and Windows platforms. The server offers features including coherence caching, Web Services management, and comprehensive JMX monitoring. WebLogic versions 12c and 14c are certified, making it the preferred option for organizations invested in Oracle technology stacks seeking full Oracle ecosystem integration.

components.name: JBoss
components.description: Red Hat JBoss EAP (Enterprise Application Platform) has been supported since 2009 as an open-source JEE application server. It provides enterprise features including clustering, management console, and Red Hat support while based on the WildFly open-source project. JBoss integrates with TOCF for Transact connectivity and supports deployment on Linux and Windows. The server is commonly paired with PostgreSQL in cost-effective stack configurations. JBoss EAP 7.x is certified, offering organizations seeking open-source alternatives with commercial support a viable enterprise deployment platform.

components.name: Tomcat
components.description: Apache Tomcat was supported from 2004 to 2016 as a lightweight servlet container for development and smaller deployments. It provided basic web application hosting without full JEE capabilities, suitable for testing environments and simple channel applications. Tomcat supported HTTP connectivity but lacked enterprise features like EJB containers, advanced clustering, and transaction management found in full JEE servers. Support was discontinued as TOCF standardized on full JEE application servers (WebSphere, WebLogic, JBoss) that provide the enterprise capabilities required for production banking deployments.

components.name: Red Hat PAM
components.description: Red Hat PAM (Process Automation Manager) was integrated into the Temenos stack in 2021 for advanced business rules and decision management. It provides a rules engine, decision tables, and business process modeling capabilities that complement Transact's Process Workflow functionality. Red Hat PAM enables complex credit decisioning, pricing calculations, and regulatory compliance rules to be externalized and managed by business users. The platform supports DMN (Decision Model and Notation) standards for portable decision logic. Integration with Temenos supports scenarios requiring sophisticated rule processing beyond core banking capabilities, particularly in lending origination and risk assessment workflows.

components.name: Kubernetes
components.description: Kubernetes container orchestration support was introduced in 2020, enabling cloud-native deployment of Transact on containerized infrastructure. The platform provides automated scaling, self-healing, rolling deployments, and declarative configuration for Temenos workloads. Kubernetes support includes Helm charts for standardized deployment, ConfigMaps for configuration management, and Secrets for credential handling. The orchestration platform enables horizontal scaling of Transact pods based on demand, improving resource efficiency and availability. Kubernetes deployment became the foundation for modern SaaS offerings, supporting deployment across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-premises infrastructure with consistent operations.

components.name: AKS
components.description: AKS (Azure Kubernetes Service) is Microsoft Azure's managed Kubernetes platform, supported for Temenos deployments since 2019. It provides automated cluster management, integrated monitoring, and Azure-native security for running Transact containers. AKS integrates with Azure SQL Database, Azure CosmosDB, and Azure Blob Storage for complete cloud solutions. The platform offers Azure Active Directory integration for identity management and Azure DevOps for CI/CD pipelines. AKS deployment supports auto-scaling, zone redundancy, and Azure-specific networking features. It became a primary deployment target for banks choosing Microsoft cloud infrastructure for their Transact implementations.

components.name: GKE
components.description: GKE (Google Kubernetes Engine) is Google Cloud's managed Kubernetes service, supported for Temenos deployments since 2019. It provides enterprise-grade container orchestration with Google's infrastructure, offering features like autopilot mode for simplified operations and tight integration with Cloud SQL and Cloud Spanner databases. GKE supports Temenos workloads with automatic scaling, multi-zone deployment, and Google Cloud's global network. The platform integrates with Google's observability tools including Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Logging. GKE became a strategic platform for banks selecting Google Cloud, providing consistent Kubernetes experience with Google's security and compliance certifications.

components.name: EKS
components.description: Amazon EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service) is the managed Kubernetes platform on AWS, officially certified for Temenos Transact deployments from 2023. EKS provides enterprise-grade Kubernetes with AWS-managed control plane, automatic updates, and deep integration with AWS services. It supports Transact containerized deployments with access to Amazon RDS, Aurora, S3, and other AWS services. EKS complements Fargate for serverless container execution and integrates with AWS load balancers, IAM, and VPC for secure banking workloads. The managed service reduces operational overhead compared to self-managed Kubernetes while maintaining compatibility with standard Kubernetes tooling.

components.name: Fargate
components.description: AWS Fargate is the serverless container compute service supported for Temenos deployments since 2019. It runs containers without managing underlying EC2 instances, providing simplified operations for Transact workloads. Fargate integrates with Amazon EKS for Kubernetes orchestration and supports AWS services including RDS, Aurora, and DynamoDB. The serverless model automatically provisions compute resources based on container requirements, eliminating capacity planning. Fargate charges based on actual resource consumption rather than provisioned capacity, offering cost optimization for variable banking workloads. It provides AWS security features including VPC isolation, IAM roles, and AWS PrivateLink for secure connectivity.

components.name: Docker
components.description: Docker container support was introduced in 2019 as part of Temenos's cloud-native transformation. Docker enables packaging of Transact components into portable, isolated containers that run consistently across development, testing, and production environments. Containerization simplified deployment by bundling TAFJ runtime, application code, and dependencies into standardized images. Docker containers are orchestrated through Kubernetes (AKS, GKE, EKS, OpenShift) for production deployments. The container approach enables microservices architecture, horizontal scaling, and immutable infrastructure patterns essential for modern banking operations.

components.name: AWS
components.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS) became a certified cloud platform for Temenos Transact in 2019. AWS provides comprehensive cloud infrastructure including compute (EC2, Fargate, EKS), database (RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB), storage (S3, EBS), and networking services. Temenos supports both Infrastructure-as-a-Service and managed Kubernetes (EKS) deployment models on AWS. The platform offers global reach with multiple regions for data residency requirements, enterprise security certifications (SOC, PCI DSS, ISO 27001), and financial services-specific compliance. AWS became one of the primary cloud platforms for Temenos SaaS and customer-managed cloud deployments.

components.name: Azure
components.description: Microsoft Azure became a certified cloud platform for Temenos Transact in 2019, offering managed Kubernetes through AKS and database services including Azure SQL and CosmosDB. Azure provides enterprise integration with Microsoft ecosystem products and strong presence in financial services markets. The platform supports hybrid cloud scenarios through Azure Arc and Azure Stack, enabling banks to maintain on-premises workloads while leveraging cloud services. Azure's compliance certifications and regional availability support global banking operations with data sovereignty requirements. Azure became a primary cloud platform alongside AWS for Temenos deployments.

components.name: GCP
components.description: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) became a certified cloud platform for Temenos Transact in 2019. GCP provides Kubernetes orchestration through GKE (Google Kubernetes Engine), which benefits from Google's deep Kubernetes expertise as the original creator of the technology. Database options include Cloud SQL, Cloud Spanner for globally distributed SQL, and BigQuery for analytics. GCP offers strong data analytics and machine learning capabilities that complement banking operations. The platform provides financial services compliance certifications and global infrastructure for international banking deployments.

components.name: Alibaba Cloud
components.description: Alibaba Cloud became a certified cloud platform for Temenos Transact in 2020 as part of the multi-cloud expansion. It provides Kubernetes orchestration through ACK (Alibaba Container Service for Kubernetes) and database services through ApsaraDB. Alibaba Cloud is particularly important for deployments in China and Asia-Pacific regions where AWS and Azure may have limited presence or regulatory restrictions. The platform offers comprehensive infrastructure services including compute (ECS), storage (OSS, Cloud Disk), and networking. Alibaba Cloud's certification enabled Temenos to address the Chinese banking market and global banks with operations in mainland China.

components.name: Huawei Cloud
components.description: Huawei Cloud became a certified cloud platform for Temenos Transact in 2020. It provides Kubernetes orchestration through CCE (Cloud Container Engine) and database services through GaussDB. Huawei Cloud serves banks in regions where Huawei has strong presence, particularly in China, Middle East, and parts of Africa. The platform offers infrastructure services including Elastic Cloud Server (ECS), Elastic Volume Service (EVS), and Object Storage Service (OBS). Huawei Cloud certification expanded Temenos's multi-cloud strategy to serve banks with geopolitical or regulatory requirements for non-Western cloud providers.

components.name: Openshift
components.description: OpenShift (Red Hat OpenShift) is an enterprise Kubernetes platform supported for Temenos deployments since 2020. It provides additional security, developer tools, and operational features on top of Kubernetes, appealing to enterprises with existing Red Hat infrastructure. OpenShift integrates with Red Hat's ecosystem including RHEL, Ansible, and middleware products. The platform offers enhanced security through Security Context Constraints, built-in CI/CD with OpenShift Pipelines, and developer self-service capabilities. OpenShift supports both on-premises and cloud deployment (Azure Red Hat OpenShift, ROSA on AWS), enabling hybrid cloud strategies for banks requiring data residency control.

components.name: IBM Cloud
components.description: IBM Cloud became a certified cloud platform for Temenos Transact in 2022. It provides Kubernetes orchestration through IBM Kubernetes Service (IKS) and Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud, along with database services including Db2 on Cloud and IBM Cloud Databases for PostgreSQL. IBM Cloud serves banks with existing IBM infrastructure investments, offering integration with IBM's broader enterprise software ecosystem including WebSphere and MQ. The platform provides financial services-specific compliance certifications and IBM's enterprise support model. IBM Cloud certification expanded deployment options for banks in regulated industries preferring IBM's enterprise governance.

components.name: Oracle Cloud
components.description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) became a certified cloud platform for Temenos Transact in 2022. It provides Kubernetes orchestration through Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) and database services through Oracle Autonomous Database and Oracle Database Cloud Service. Oracle Cloud serves banks with significant Oracle database investments, offering optimized performance for Oracle DB workloads and integration with Oracle's middleware stack including WebLogic. The platform provides enterprise security features, dedicated regions for regulated industries, and Oracle's enterprise support. OCI certification enabled seamless cloud migration for banks running Transact on Oracle infrastructure.

components.name: TEC
components.description: TEC (T24 Enterprise Console) was a comprehensive system management framework introduced in T24 R07 (2007), built to internet standards. It provided a robust console with a rich set of tools to detect, solve, and simplify operational problems in T24 environments. TEC allowed users to monitor every aspect of performance and behavior by defining monitoring profiles that reported on system use and activity. Features included graphical displays with full drilldown and investigative facilities, exception management tools, and historical reporting capabilities. Access was via the COS TEC command. TEC was replaced by tOP (Temenos Operations Platform) in 2015-2016 which provided more modern monitoring capabilities.

components.name: tOP
components.description: tOP (Temenos Operations Platform) was the operational monitoring and management platform from 2015 to 2023. It provided infrastructure monitoring, application health checks, and operational dashboards for Temenos deployments. tOP included capabilities for log aggregation, performance metrics collection, and alerting for production banking environments. The platform supported both on-premises and cloud deployments, offering visibility into system health and resource utilization. tOP was replaced by Grafana-based observability in 2021-2023 as Temenos adopted industry-standard monitoring tools. This transition aligned with cloud-native architecture patterns and provided better integration with Kubernetes environments.

components.name: Grafana
components.description: Grafana is the observability and monitoring platform adopted by Temenos in 2021, replacing the proprietary tOP platform. It provides dashboards, alerting, and visualization for Transact deployments across metrics, logs, and traces. Grafana integrates with Prometheus for metrics collection, Loki for log aggregation, and Tempo for distributed tracing, forming a complete observability stack. The platform supports custom dashboards for banking-specific metrics including transaction rates, response times, and system health. Grafana's open-source foundation enables integration with cloud-native monitoring tools and Kubernetes-native service discovery. It became the standard observability solution for SaaS and cloud deployments.

components.name: Stack Tiers
components.description: Stack Tiers is the tiered support model introduced in 2024 for deployment configurations. It categorizes database, application server, and operating system combinations into support levels: Tier 1 (full support and certification for production), Tier 2 (supported with limited testing for non-production), and Tier 3 (community support for development). This model helps customers understand which configurations receive the highest support priority and testing investment. Stack Tiers guide technology decisions by clearly indicating strategic versus legacy deployment options, encouraging migration toward cloud-native configurations while maintaining support for established enterprise stacks.

components.name: Queueless Option
components.description: The Queueless Option, introduced in 2022, enables direct HTTP-based integration between Transact and external systems without requiring message queue infrastructure. This simplified integration pattern replaces the traditional flow (External to MQ to Adapter to Transact) with direct HTTP communication enhanced by built-in retry logic and circuit breaker patterns. Configuration includes retry attempts, backoff intervals, failure thresholds, and reset timeouts for fault tolerance. The Queueless Option reduces architectural complexity and infrastructure costs for organizations that do not require the guaranteed delivery and buffering capabilities of message queues. It provides lower latency for synchronous operations while maintaining reliability through robust error handling mechanisms built into the HTTP layer.

components.name: Rapid Packaging
components.description: Rapid Packaging is a Temenos technology that modularizes Transact by packaging JBC subroutines (Java classes with TAFJ) into optimized JAR files for specific business functions. It analyzes OFS requests and packages only the necessary subroutines, bypassing the TEMPLATE layer for improved performance. Rapid uses two tools: OFSRequester for executing and validating OFS request scripts, and RapidPackager for generating two JAR files - a TransactCommon.jar (shared classes) and a Specific.jar (use-case specific classes). Key benefits include reduced deployment size, faster startup times, lower cost per transaction, and improved scalability through modular Transact deployments.

components.name: ServLite
components.description: ServLite enables Transact to run without traditional application servers (WebSphere, WebLogic, JBoss), providing a lightweight runtime for cloud-native deployments. For batch pods, it replaces the app server with a program that starts TSA agents directly at container startup, reducing startup time from ~150 seconds to ~32 seconds. For IRIS, it enables direct invocation of TemnClientAPI without EJB layers or queues. ServLite includes Transact Scaler for Kubernetes-based auto-scaling using KEDA and Prometheus metrics. Benefits include smaller hardware requirements, faster container startup for dynamic scaling, simplified architecture, reduced third-party dependencies, and improved cloud-native compatibility.

components.name: Green Screen
components.description: Green Screen was the original terminal-based interface introduced in 1985, providing character-based user interaction with the EBS and early Globus banking systems. Users interacted through monochrome displays with keyboard-driven navigation using function keys for commands like F1=Help, F3=Exit, and F10=Menu. The interface displayed banking screens in fixed-format layouts typical of mainframe-era computing. This technology served as the primary channel for bank tellers and back-office operations until graphical interfaces emerged in 1994. Green Screen remained in use through 1998 before being fully replaced by GUI-based desktop clients.

components.name: GUI v1
components.description: GUI v1 was Temenos's first graphical user interface introduced in 1994 for Windows 3.1 environments. It marked the transition from character-based green screen terminals to visual desktop applications with basic forms and menu navigation. The interface featured limited graphics capabilities constrained by the Windows 3.1 platform but represented a significant improvement in usability for bank staff. GUI v1 was replaced within two years by GUI v2, which leveraged the enhanced capabilities of Windows 95.

components.name: GUI v2
components.description: GUI v2 was the second generation graphical interface released in 1996 for Windows 95 platforms. It featured improved layouts, enhanced navigation, and print capabilities compared to its predecessor. The interface coincided with the introduction of OFS (Open Financial Service), enabling better integration between the desktop client and external systems. GUI v2 provided a more polished user experience aligned with Windows 95 design standards and served bank operations for two years before GUI v3 arrived in 1998.

components.name: GUI v3
components.description: GUI v3 was the third and most mature generation of the original desktop GUI series, introduced in 1998 for Windows NT environments. It achieved full feature parity with the underlying Globus core banking system and offered customizable layouts along with enhanced reporting capabilities. This version represented the peak of the first-generation Windows desktop clients before the transition to VB Desktop in 2000. GUI v3 established many user interaction patterns that would influence subsequent Temenos channel development.

components.name: VB Desktop
components.description: VB Desktop was a Visual Basic-based desktop client introduced in 2000 that provided a rich Windows application experience for bank staff. Built using Microsoft Visual Basic technology, it offered improved performance and a more modern interface compared to earlier GUI versions. VB Desktop coincided with the JBase/TAFC platform-independent runtime layer introduction, enabling deployment across multiple operating systems. The client remained in production use until 2013 when browser-based interfaces became the preferred approach for core banking access.

components.name: .NET Desktop
components.description: .NET Desktop was a Microsoft .NET-based desktop client introduced in 2007 as an alternative to VB Desktop. Built on the .NET Framework, it provided modern Windows application capabilities with improved integration into Microsoft enterprise environments. The client offered enhanced performance and security features compared to the aging VB Desktop platform. .NET Desktop was retired in 2014 as Temenos shifted strategic focus toward browser-based interfaces that eliminated the need for client-side software installation.

components.name: jIBI
components.description: jIBI (Java Internet Banking Interface) was Temenos's first web-based internet banking solution, introduced in 2000. It used Java applet technology requiring browser plugins to deliver banking functionality to end customers. While pioneering in bringing banking to the web, the Java applet approach had limitations including plugin requirements, security concerns, and performance issues. jIBI was replaced by GIB (Globus Internet Banking) in 2002, which adopted server-side JSP rendering for improved compatibility and user experience.

components.name: GIB
components.description: GIB (Globus Internet Banking) was a JSP-based web application introduced in 2002 that provided full browser support for internet banking. Unlike its predecessor jIBI, GIB used server-side rendering eliminating the need for Java browser plugins. The platform offered broader functionality, enhanced security, and better performance through its modern web architecture. GIB served as Temenos's primary internet banking solution during the late Globus and early T24 era before being replaced by TCIB (Temenos Connect Internet Banking) in 2012.

components.name: TIB
components.description: TIB (Temenos Internet Banking) was introduced in 2004 alongside the T24 rebranding, providing a modern web design for internet banking integrated with the T24 core banking system. It featured expanded functionality compared to GIB, including multi-language support and improved user interfaces. TIB served customers during the middle T24 era, offering secure online banking capabilities. The platform was superseded by TCIB in 2012 as Temenos consolidated its internet banking offerings into a unified platform.

components.name: BrowserWeb
components.description: BrowserWeb was the standard T24 web browser interface introduced in 2004, providing browser-based access to T24 core banking functionality. It replaced earlier terminal-based and desktop GUI interfaces, enabling bank staff to access T24 through standard web browsers. BrowserWeb delivered server-rendered HTML pages with T24 enquiries, transactions, and data entry screens accessible via any web browser. The interface supported T24's workflow and transaction processing while enabling deployment without client-side software installation. Neo Browser was intended to replace BrowserWeb with a richer interface, but Flash limitations led to BrowserWeb remaining in use until UXP Browser provided a modern HTML5 alternative in 2016.

components.name: ARC-IB
components.description: ARC-IB (Arc Internet Banking) was an advanced internet banking platform introduced in 2008 based on the edgeIPK technology. It featured a widget-based architecture enabling highly customizable banking experiences with enhanced user experience capabilities. ARC-IB represented a step forward in web banking sophistication, allowing banks to create differentiated digital experiences. The platform was consolidated into TCIB (Temenos Connect Internet Banking) in 2012 as part of Temenos's channel rationalization strategy.

components.name: Neo Browser
components.description: Neo Browser was a Rich Internet Application (RIA) introduced in 2010 built on Adobe Flash/Flex technology. It was originally intended to replace the earlier BrowserWeb interface with a more sophisticated desktop-like user experience. Neo Browser delivered rich visual interfaces with smooth animations and complex UI components impossible with pure HTML at the time, using Flash's advanced graphics capabilities. However, the platform never fully replaced BrowserWeb as intended due to Flash's declining browser support and security concerns. Neo Browser was deprecated and retired by 2016 as Adobe Flash approached end-of-life, with users eventually migrating to UXP Browser which was built on modern web standards.

components.name: TCIB
components.description: TCIB (Temenos Connect Internet Banking) was launched in 2012 as Temenos's flagship internet banking platform. Built on HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, it featured responsive design supporting multiple devices without requiring plugins. TCIB integrated with T24 through IRIS APIs, providing secure authentication, comprehensive transaction processing, account management, payments, and transfers. The platform served as the primary web banking channel until 2020 when it was superseded by Infinity for new deployments, though it remains active for existing installations.

components.name: UXP Browser
components.description: UXP Browser was the web interface component of the User Experience Platform, introduced in 2016 as a replacement for Neo Browser and BrowserWeb, retired in 2024. Built on modern web standards without Flash dependencies, it delivered rich banking experiences through HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. UXP Browser provided responsive design supporting desktop, tablet, and mobile form factors within a single codebase. The platform offered extensive customization through the UXP widget library and theme engine, enabling banks to create branded digital experiences. UXP Browser was superseded by Transact Explorer in 2024 as the modern web interface for Transact core banking operations.

components.name: Transact Explorer
components.description: Transact Explorer is the auto-generated user interface for Temenos Transact, introduced in 2022, primarily for back-office bank employee use. Built from metadata definitions, it enables rapid creation of new UI components - a new database view can be configured using metadata within minutes and automatically renders in the UI. Transact Explorer supports role-based access with over 40 out-of-the-box role-specific homepages tailored to typical banking profiles. These views can be customized or new ones created using metadata. All user interfaces including Transact Explorer are accessible through Temenos Explorer, providing consistent look and feel with single sign-on. Starting in 2024, it replaced UXP Browser as the primary browser interface for Transact operations.

components.name: Temenos Explorer
components.description: Temenos Explorer is a unified access platform introduced in 2023 that provides a consistent and seamless user experience across various Temenos banking solutions - a single pane of glass. It acts as a wrapper consolidating different user interfaces including the auto-generated Transact Explorer and hand-crafted user agents built with Temenos Unified UX (UUX) technology. Through Temenos Explorer, users access multiple applications with single sign-on, ensuring streamlined workflow and consistent look and feel. It supports role-based homepages tailored to specific user profiles, serving both configuration and operational needs. Temenos Explorer integrates with Keycloak for authentication and supports multi-language capabilities with bank branding customization.

components.name: TCMB
components.description: TCMB (Temenos Connect Mobile Banking) was introduced in 2013 as Temenos's dedicated mobile banking platform. It provided native iOS and Android applications with biometric authentication, push notifications, offline capability, and camera integration for features like mobile check deposit. TCMB delivered native mobile performance while maintaining integration with T24/Transact through IRIS APIs. The platform was superseded by Infinity in 2020 as part of Temenos's digital front-office modernization, though legacy installations continue operating.

components.name: Online Banking
components.description: Temenos Infinity Online Banking is a comprehensive digital banking solution designed to deliver seamless, personalized, and secure online banking experiences. It supports a wide range of banking services including account management, payments, transfers, loan applications, and investment services. Built to be highly configurable and extensible, it allows banks to tailor the user experience to their specific brand and customer needs without heavy reliance on IT development. Key features include responsive design for accessibility on various devices, integration with Temenos core banking systems and third-party services via open APIs, and strong security measures such as multi-factor authentication and compliance with regulatory standards like PSD2. The platform supports advanced personalization, AI-driven insights, and real-time interactions, enhancing customer engagement and satisfaction.

components.name: Native Mobile
components.description: Native Mobile refers to Temenos's native iOS and Android mobile applications introduced in 2019 as part of the Infinity platform. These applications provide device-optimized experiences leveraging platform-specific capabilities including biometric authentication (Touch ID, Face ID), push notifications, and camera integration. Native Mobile apps are built using Quantum Fabric's multi-experience development capabilities, enabling code sharing while maintaining native performance. The applications deliver consumer-grade mobile banking experiences integrated with Transact or third-party core systems.

components.name: Quantum User Agents
components.description: Quantum User Agents are channel-specific applications introduced in 2022 built on Quantum Fabric technology. They provide optimized user experiences for specific devices and contexts including mobile phones, tablets, and wearables. User Agents leverage Quantum Fabric's multi-experience capabilities to deliver consistent functionality across platforms while adapting to device-specific interaction patterns. The agents support offline operation, biometric authentication, and push notifications while maintaining synchronization with backend systems.

components.name: edgeIPK
components.description: edgeIPK was a UI platform introduced in 2012 that served as the precursor to UXP. It featured a widget-based architecture enabling component-based development of banking interfaces. edgeIPK powered the ARC-IB internet banking solution and introduced concepts that would later evolve into the UXP platform. The technology was retired in 2016 when UXP emerged as the strategic replacement, incorporating edgeIPK's architectural principles into a more modern framework aligned with HTML5 web standards.

components.name: UXP
components.description: UXP (User Experience Platform) was introduced in 2016 as a comprehensive framework for building digital banking experiences. It features a widget library with pre-built components for accounts, payments, charts, and alerts, along with a theme engine for branding customization. UXP includes a navigation framework for managing menus, workflows, and screen flows. The platform supports responsive layouts and provides a graphical product builder for configuring banking applications. UXP remains active and serves as a foundation for both web and agent desktop interfaces.

components.name: UUX
components.description: UUX (Unified User Experience) was introduced in 2022 as a framework for delivering consistent banking experiences across all Temenos channels. It provides standardized design patterns, components, and interaction models that work across Infinity, Transact Explorer, and mobile applications. UUX ensures brand consistency and usability standards while reducing development effort through reusable components. The framework supports accessibility requirements and responsive design principles for modern digital banking.

components.name: Product and Pricing Designer
components.description: Product AMD Designer is a visual design tool introduced in 2022 for configuring Arrangement Architecture product definitions. It provides a graphical interface for creating and modifying banking products using the AMD (Arrangement Model Definition) framework, enabling business analysts to design product structures, properties, and behaviors without deep technical knowledge. The tool supports drag-and-drop component assembly, property configuration, and product simulation capabilities. Product AMD Designer integrates with Design Studio and Workbench development environments, streamlining the product configuration workflow from design through deployment.

components.name: UXP Agents
components.description: UXP Agents is the agent desktop interface component introduced in 2018, providing bank staff with a unified workspace for customer service operations. Built on the UXP framework, it delivers a modern, widget-based interface for tellers, relationship managers, and contact center agents. UXP Agents consolidates customer information, transaction capabilities, and workflow tools into a single application. The platform supports role-based views and integrates with core banking systems through Temenos APIs to streamline branch and call center operations.

components.name: LO24
components.description: LO24 was a lending origination module introduced in 2009 that provided workflows for loan application processing within T24. It handled credit applications, underwriting workflows, decision management, and disbursement processes. LO24 supported various lending products including consumer loans, mortgages, and commercial lending. The module was superseded by Origination Architecture in 2015 and eventually by Infinity Onboarding and Origination as Temenos modernized its origination capabilities.

components.name: Treasury Trader
components.description: Treasury Trader was a specialized trading interface introduced in 2010 for treasury operations and financial markets activities. It provided real-time market data integration, trade execution capabilities, and position management for treasury dealers. The module supported foreign exchange, money market, and securities trading operations. Treasury Trader was retired in 2017 as treasury functionality was consolidated into core T24 modules and external specialized trading systems.

components.name: Origination Architecture
components.description: Origination Architecture was introduced in 2018 as a framework for digital product origination workflows. It provided configurable journeys for loan applications, account opening, and other banking product origination scenarios. The architecture supported integration with credit bureaus, document management systems, and decision engines. Origination Architecture was superseded by Infinity Onboarding and Origination in 2019 as part of the broader Infinity platform launch.

components.name: TFO
components.description: TFO (Temenos Financial Operations) was introduced in 2018 as a specialized interface for financial operations and treasury management. It provided dedicated workflows for back-office operations including trade processing, settlement, and reconciliation. TFO offered role-specific views optimized for operations teams handling complex financial transactions. The platform was retired in 2021 as its functionality was absorbed into broader platform capabilities within Infinity and Transact Explorer.

components.name: Infinity
components.description: Infinity is Temenos's digital front-office platform launched in 2019 as part of the Transact/Infinity product split. It provides omnichannel digital banking experiences across web, mobile, tablet, wearable, and conversational interfaces. Built on Quantum Fabric (MXDP), Infinity can operate standalone or integrated with Transact core banking. The platform includes microservices for party management, holdings, payments, and onboarding. Infinity features journey analytics, low-code application development through Maestro, and visual design tools through Infinity Visualizer.

components.name: Infinity Microservices
components.description: Infinity Microservices is a collection of modular, independently deployable services that power the Temenos Infinity platform as a standalone distribution engine. Introduced in 2020, these microservices enable banks to build, extend, and customize digital channels and customer journeys with agility and scalability. The microservices handle discrete business capabilities including party management, holdings, payments, and onboarding, communicating through APIs and event-driven mechanisms. They leverage a cloud-native architecture with loose coupling, API-first design, and event-driven communication. While still available, Infinity Microservices are primarily used by larger clients requiring standalone Infinity deployments without Transact core banking.

components.name: Spotlight
components.description: Temenos Spotlight is a back-office and administration tool introduced in 2020 for self-servicing digital channels. It enables bank users such as contact center agents to efficiently manage customer information without accessing the core banking system directly. After logging in, authorized users with sufficient rights can access Customer Management to search for customers using various criteria. Within the customer view, users can edit personal details including address, phone, email, preferred communication methods, marital status, and employment status. Integration with Temenos Transact is automatic, ensuring updates synchronize without separate core banking access. Spotlight supports configuration flexibility, allowing banks to define visible elements in customer journeys and update settings in real-time.

components.name: Journey Analytics
components.description: Journey Analytics was introduced in 2020 as part of the Infinity platform, originating from Temenos's Avoka acquisition. It provided insights into customer digital journeys, tracking user sessions, page views, and actions to measure engagement and identify friction points. Features included conversion funnel analysis showing where customers abandoned applications, A/B testing capabilities for optimizing journey variants, cohort analysis for user segments, and real-time dashboards. Journey Analytics helped banks optimize digital experiences by identifying drop-off points and improvement opportunities in onboarding and origination processes. The capability was consolidated into broader Infinity analytics offerings in 2021.

components.name: TJM
components.description: TJM (Temenos Journey Manager) is a journey orchestration platform introduced in 2020, originating from Temenos's acquisition of Avoka Technologies in 2019. It enables banks to design and manage complex customer journeys for onboarding, loan applications, account opening, and other multi-step processes. TJM provides visual journey design tools, form builders, workflow orchestration, state tracking, and integration with backend systems including Transact. The platform supports both digital self-service journeys and assisted journeys with bank staff involvement. TJM's capabilities came from Avoka's digital acquisition platform, which specialized in customer journey automation for financial services.

components.name: Quantum Fabric
components.description: Quantum Fabric is the Multi-experience Development Platform (MXDP) underlying Infinity, introduced in 2020 following Temenos's acquisition of Kony. It provides identity services (authentication, SSO, MFA), integration services (API orchestration, data sync), engagement services (push notifications, campaigns), and analytics services (user behavior, journey analytics). Quantum Fabric includes offline data synchronization capabilities and a Fabric Console for administration and monitoring. The platform enables rapid development of omnichannel banking applications.

components.name: Quantum Visualizer
components.description: Infinity Visualizer is a visual design tool for creating digital banking experiences, introduced in 2020. It provides a drag-and-drop interface for designing customer journeys, configuring widgets, and managing screen flows. The tool includes preview and testing capabilities allowing designers to validate experiences before deployment. Infinity Visualizer supports deployment automation, enabling seamless publishing of designed experiences to production channels. It empowers business users to customize banking interfaces without extensive coding knowledge.

components.name: Maestro
components.description: Maestro is a low-code form and journey builder introduced in 2019 as part of Temenos's Avoka acquisition. It enables rapid creation of digital banking applications, forms, and customer journeys through visual drag-and-drop configuration rather than traditional coding. Maestro provides pre-built form components, validation rules, conditional logic, document upload widgets, and e-signature integration that can be assembled to create customer onboarding flows, loan applications, and service requests. The tool integrates with TJM for journey orchestration and connects to Transact for backend processing. Maestro democratizes application development, allowing business users to build and modify digital experiences with minimal IT involvement.

components.name: Payments Cockpit
components.description: Payments Cockpit is a specialized payments operations interface introduced in 2024 as a plug-in within Temenos Explorer. Built on the UUX platform, it provides dashboard widgets including Cut-Off Time Monitor, Case Management, Business Activity Monitor, and STP Rate tracking. The interface manages payment queues for authorizations, external responses, future-dated payments, and clearing dispatch. It supports MT and MX format case management for cancellations, investigations, and modifications. Payments Cockpit integrates with Holdings microservice via event streaming for high-performance payment data queries, enabling role-based access and centralized payment operations visibility.

components.name: Assist
components.description: Assist is a Temenos Digital back-office solution introduced in 2021 that supports retail, business, and commercial customer onboarding and origination journeys. It provides banking operatives with tools to manage the end-to-end application lifecycle from request capture through to funding, with dynamic task assignment, multi-channel request monitoring, stage management queues, and third-party integration support for credit assessments and risk analysis.

components.name: Infinity Onboarding and Origination
components.description: Infinity Onboarding and Origination is a digital customer acquisition solution introduced in 2021. It provides end-to-end workflows for customer onboarding including identity verification, KYC/AML checks, document collection, and account opening. For product origination, it supports loan applications, credit checks, and approval workflows. The solution integrates with Infinity's journey management and analytics capabilities to optimize conversion rates. It replaced the earlier Origination Architecture and supports both fully digital and assisted origination processes.

components.name: VCOO
components.description: VCOO (Virtual COO) was an AI-powered operations intelligence tool introduced in 2021. It provided automated insights and recommendations for optimizing banking operations, identifying inefficiencies, and suggesting process improvements. VCOO leveraged machine learning to analyze operational data and surface actionable intelligence for operations leadership. The tool was retired in 2023 as its capabilities were integrated into broader analytics and AI offerings within the Temenos platform.

components.name: Infinity Digital for Salesforce
components.description: Infinity Digital for Salesforce was introduced in 2021 to embed banking capabilities within Salesforce CRM. It provided relationship managers with customer financial views, product recommendations, and service actions directly in their familiar Salesforce interface. The integration streamlined sales and service processes for banks using Salesforce as their CRM platform. The solution was retired in 2024 as banks moved toward more integrated platform approaches.

components.name: CLOS
components.description: CLOS (Corporate Lending Origination System) was acquired in 2023 to allow banks to digitally initiate Credit Applications for corporate customers. It offered a flexible platform for creating credit applications, performing risk assessments, and approving credit packages via configurable workflows. Abandoned in 2025.

components.name: SMS
components.description: SMS (Security Management System) is T24/Transact's core security infrastructure managing user authentication, authorization, and session control. Introduced in 1999 during the Globus era, SMS handles password policies including complexity requirements, expiration rules, and failed attempt lockouts. It manages user profiles with role-based access assignments, controlling which applications, screens, and functions each user can access. SMS maintains audit trails of user activities for regulatory compliance, tracking login attempts, session durations, and transaction authorizations. The system supports multi-level authorization workflows where sensitive transactions require approval from multiple users. SMS integrates with external authentication providers and forms the foundation upon which newer security components like XACML and Keycloak build additional capabilities.

components.name: XACML
components.description: XACML (eXtensible Access Control Markup Language) provides attribute-based access control for Temenos Transact, introduced in 2019 as part of the cloud-native security layer. Unlike traditional role-based access, XACML enables fine-grained authorization decisions based on multiple attributes including user context, resource properties, environmental conditions, and action types. The system uses an external policy server where authorization policies are defined in standardized XML format. When access requests occur, XACML evaluates policies to determine permit or deny decisions. This approach supports complex banking scenarios such as transaction limits based on customer segment, time-based restrictions, geographic controls, and regulatory compliance requirements. XACML complements existing SMS capabilities with modern policy-driven security.

components.name: Entitlements
components.description: Entitlements was a read-only microservice introduced in 2019 that held the list of entitlements (permissions) a user has on entities such as accounts, contracts, customers, and payment orders. It was designed to work alongside XACML for fine-grained, resource-level access control in the microservices architecture. The service was intended to enable granular authorization checks at the entity level rather than just role-based access. However, Entitlements was never widely adopted and the functionality it was meant to provide remained within Infinity and Spotlight platforms. The microservice was retired in 2024 without achieving its original vision of XACML-based resource-level authorization.

components.name: Traceability
components.description: Traceability is Temenos's audit and compliance tracking service introduced in 2019 for the Transact cloud-native platform. The component provides comprehensive transaction tracing capabilities, capturing detailed audit logs of all system activities including API calls, data modifications, user sessions, and business events. Traceability supports regulatory compliance requirements by maintaining immutable records of who did what, when, and from where. The service enables banks to generate compliance reports, investigate security incidents, and demonstrate regulatory adherence to auditors. It integrates with the observability stack including Grafana for visualization and analysis of audit data. Traceability supports distributed tracing across microservices, correlating activities across multiple system components. The service was active from 2019 to 2024.

components.name: Keycloak
components.description: Keycloak is the open-source identity and access management solution integrated into Temenos Transact starting in 2020. It provides enterprise-grade authentication services including OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocols for secure token-based access. Keycloak enables Single Sign-On (SSO) across Transact applications, allowing users to authenticate once and access multiple services seamlessly. The platform supports identity federation, connecting to external identity providers such as corporate Active Directory, LDAP, and social login providers.
