Keycloak manages user sessions, implements token refresh mechanisms, and handles secure logout across distributed applications. It integrates with the Kubernetes-based deployment model, providing containerized identity services that scale with the platform and supporting multi-tenant banking environments.

components.name: SaaS 1.0
components.description: SaaS 1.0 (2011-2020) was Temenos' first cloud-hosted banking service offering, initially launched to serve the microfinance sector. It provided managed T24 deployments in Temenos-operated data centers, handling infrastructure provisioning, system updates, and daily operations on behalf of client banks. This model enabled smaller financial institutions to access enterprise-grade core banking capabilities without significant capital investment in IT infrastructure or specialized technical staff. SaaS 1.0 operated on traditional virtual machine infrastructure with shared or dedicated tenancy options, laying the groundwork for Temenos' cloud strategy before being superseded by the cloud-native SaaS 2.0 architecture.

components.name: Trinovus
components.description: Trinovus (2014-2016) was a specialized SaaS banking solution developed by Temenos specifically for the US community banking market. Acquired to accelerate Temenos' penetration into North America, Trinovus offered a pre-configured, cloud-hosted core banking platform tailored to American regulatory requirements including Fed integration, ACH processing, and US-specific compliance needs. The solution provided community banks and credit unions with modern banking technology without the complexity of traditional core system implementations. Trinovus was eventually integrated into the broader Temenos product portfolio, with its US market-specific functionality incorporated into subsequent platform versions.

components.name: SaaS 2.0
components.description: SaaS 2.0 (2020-2023) represented Temenos' transition to cloud-native architecture for its managed service offering. Built on Kubernetes container orchestration, it enabled elastic horizontal scaling, automated deployments through CI/CD pipelines, and improved multi-tenant isolation compared to its predecessor. SaaS 2.0 supported hybrid cloud deployment models across AWS, Azure, and GCP, providing banks with flexibility in choosing their cloud provider. The platform introduced enhanced DevOps integration, infrastructure-as-code practices, and improved observability through Grafana-based monitoring. SaaS 2.0 served as the transitional architecture before evolving into the more comprehensive SaaS Foundation platform.

components.name: TCD
components.description: TCD (Temenos Continuous Deployment) introduced in 2020, was a SaaS offering enabling banks to manage, configure, and assemble Temenos software with on-demand environment provisioning. TCD allowed creation of non-production environments within minutes rather than weeks, accelerating development and change projects. It divided into three processes: Extend (customization), Assemble (component assembly with CI/CD), and Deliver (deployment). The Assemble module provided DevOps capabilities for continuous integration and delivery of Temenos products and customizations, managing component assembly, test environment provisioning, test script execution, and results dashboards. TCD supported automated deployment of configuration, updates, plugins, and data through CI/CD pipelines integrated with source control. It was superseded by Integrated DevOps in 2024.

components.name: Integrated DevOps
components.description: Integrated DevOps (2024-present) is embedded within Temenos SaaS Foundation, enabling frequent, predictable, high-impact changes with minimal manual effort through CI/CD. It provides a self-service portal for provisioning and managing banking services, an engine for automated orchestration, and runtime environment deployment. The platform embraces 'Everything-as-Code' philosophy where configuration, infrastructure, security, and pipelines are managed through code in source control. It uses Infrastructure as Code (IaC) automation, Helm charts for Kubernetes deployment, and Git integration for consistent environment provisioning. Release Validation Tests (RVT) provide automated functional tests validating changes before deployment. Banks can self-manage development and testing environments while maintaining automated continuous delivery benefits.

components.name: Continuous Updates
components.description: Continuous Updates delivers software updates through monthly releases and an Annual Maintenance Release (AMR). Monthly releases provide incremental improvements and rapid access to new functionality, while AMR consolidates all yearly changes including regulatory updates and features into a stable upgrade package. The Temenos Extensibility Framework enables configuration changes and extensions in parallel with updates, embedding DevOps principles for high-impact changes with minimal manual effort. Release Validation Tests ensure resilience and stability during updates. For SaaS clients, updates are managed by Temenos with minimal disruption, including security patches, features, and regulatory changes. Clients receive advance notice and can test in sandbox environments before production deployment.

components.name: SaaS Foundation
components.description: SaaS Foundation is the enterprise cloud deployment platform introduced in 2023, representing the latest evolution of Temenos SaaS offerings. It provides a comprehensive managed service including infrastructure, application management, updates, and support under enterprise SLAs. SaaS Foundation builds on Kubernetes-based SaaS Native with additional enterprise features including advanced security controls, compliance certifications, and disaster recovery capabilities. The platform includes integrated DevOps tooling, Grafana-based observability, and automated operational procedures. SaaS Foundation supports global deployment across multiple cloud providers while meeting banking regulatory requirements for data residency and security.

components.name: Modular Workbench
components.description: Modular Workbench is an integrated, web-based development environment for configuring, extending, and customizing Temenos modular banking solutions. It supports multiple Temenos modules from a single user interface, providing a unified platform for the entire software development lifecycle (SDLC). Key features include a design tool for configurations, packager capability for deployable packages, Git integration for source control, low-code/no-code tools for rapid development, and embedded DevOps support for CI/CD. The Workbench enables banks to rapidly adapt their modular solutions while preserving upgrade paths and maintaining system reliability.

components.name: Workbench AI
components.description: Workbench AI is an AI-powered version of Temenos Workbench that leverages artificial intelligence to accelerate development workflows. It assists developers in writing extensions using Python, generating test cases automatically, and creating customizations with intelligent code suggestions. The AI capabilities enable faster development cycles, improved code quality through automated testing recommendations, and reduced learning curves for new developers.
